71	## Reading a response into a type
72	
73	### Sub-selections map over arrays for free
74	
75	There is no array syntax. A sub-selection after an array-valued path applies to
76	every element, the way a GraphQL selection set does. Every row below is
77	executed output for one response whose `author.articles` is a two-element array:
78	
79	| Selection | Result |
80	|---|---|
81	| `author.articles.title` | `["T1", "T2"]` |
82	| `author.articles { title }` | `[{title:"T1"}, {title:"T2"}]` |
83	| `author.articles.byline.place` | `["P1", "P2"]` |
84	| `author.articles { title place: byline.place }` | `[{title, place}, …]` |
85	| `author.articles { td: { title date } }` | `[{td:{title,date}}, …]` |
86	
87	If the value turns out not to be an array, the same selection yields one
88	result instead of a list. The string does not change.
89	
90	Paths inside the braces start from each element, so
91	`author.articles { name: author.name }` gives `name: null` for every article.
92	To reach the parent, bind it first:
93	`author->as($a).articles { name: $a.name }` gives `name: "Ben"` on each.
94	
95	### Separators
96	
97	A selection list is separated by whitespace or by commas, **not both**:
98	`a, b, c` and `a b c` are fine, and `a, b c` fails with a message saying the
99	list is comma-separated. Method arguments always take commas. The examples in
100	this file use whitespace, which is the only form v0.3 accepts.
101	
102	**At v0.3:** commas in a selection list are a parse error.
103	
104	### Stripping an envelope
105	
106	Most REST list endpoints wrap the payload. Select through the wrapper with `$.`
107	and keep siblings alongside it:
108	
109	```graphql
110	selection: """
111	$.data { id name }
112	nextCursor: meta.next_cursor
113	"""
114	```
115	
116	Given `{"data":{"id":7,"name":"n"},"meta":{"next_cursor":"c1"}}` this produces
117	`{id: 7, name: "n", nextCursor: "c1"}`: the `data` wrapper is gone and
118	`nextCursor` sits beside the fields it wrapped.
119	
120	### The single-key rule
121	
122	This is the one that silently produces the wrong shape.
123	
124	```graphql
125	author { name }              # keeps the key:  { author: { name } }
126	some.nested.path { a b c }   # merges:         { a, b, c }
127	```
128	
129	A **single** key with a sub-selection contributes that key to the output. A
130	path of more than one step does not, so its sub-selection merges into the
131	parent. Executed, both in one selection, the result is
132	`{author: {name: "Ben"}, a: "A", b: "B", c: "C"}`.
133	
134	Two consequences worth holding on to:
135	
136	- Adding one step flips the behaviour. `author { name }` keeps `author`;
137	  `author.details { name }` does not.
138	- To get the flat value from a single key, write `$.author { name }`. To keep
139	  a key on a longer path, alias it: `abc: some.nested.path { a b c }`.
140	
141	### Building an object the API sent flat
142	
143	When the response has `authorID` and `authorName` but the schema wants a nested
144	`author`, alias a sub-selection. The alias is required, because the group would
145	otherwise be anonymous:
146	
147	```graphql
148	selection: """
149	postID
150	title
151	author: {
152	  id: authorID
153	  name: authorName
154	}
155	"""
156	```
157	
158	### Turning an array of ids into entity references
159	
160	A very common REST shape, and three tokens:
161	
162	```graphql
163	selection: """
164	id
165	friends: friend_ids { id: $ }
166	"""
167	```
168	
169	`{"id":123,"friend_ids":[234,345,456]}` becomes
170	`{id: 123, friends: [{id:234},{id:345},{id:456}]}`. Inside the sub-selection
171	`$` is each element in turn.
172	
173	The target field has to be a typed object list. A `{ … }` group cannot target a
174	`<Prefix>_JSON` scalar: composition rejects it with
175	`GROUP_SELECTION_IS_NOT_OBJECT`. The JSON escape hatch in
176	[schema-authoring.md](schema-authoring.md) does not absorb a sub-selection.
177	
178	### Renaming snake_case keys in bulk
179	
180	`->keysToCamelCase` renames every key of an object, so one line replaces a
181	block of `camelCase: snake_case` aliases:
182	
183	```graphql
184	selection: """
185	$->keysToCamelCase { id loginName fullName }
186	"""
187	```
188	
189	turns `{"id":1,"login_name":"ben","full_name":"Ben Newman"}` into
190	`{id: 1, loginName: "ben", fullName: "Ben Newman"}`. The sub-selection is not
191	optional: without it composition cannot see which fields the method provides,
192	and every field of the type is `CONNECTORS_UNRESOLVED_FIELD`.
193	`->keysToCamelCaseDeep` recurses: `{"outer_key":{"inner_key":1}}` becomes
194	`{outerKey: {innerKey: 1}}`.
195	
196	Aliases stay the right tool when the GraphQL name is not the camelCase of the
197	wire name. [naming.md](naming.md) has the rules.
198	
199	In a factory workspace, keep the aliases for now: the tools do not yet
200	read through `->keysToCamelCase`. `graphos-factory-core reconcile` reports every
201	field it renames as unmapped; `source-coverage` reports every field under a
202	root `$->keysToCamelCase { … }` as `unaccounted`, and every field under a
203	nested one as `unresolved`.
204	
205	## Abstract types
206	
207	A `oneOf` whose members a wire value tells apart (usually a `discriminator`)
208	becomes a union, or an interface when the members share fields. One form
209	composes: a `...` spread of `->match` on the discriminator, with one arm per
210	member, each an object carrying a literal `__typename`:
211	
212	```graphql
213	type Query {
214	  media: [Media] @connect(source: "api", http: { GET: "/media" }, selection: """
215	  id
216	  title
217	  ... kind->match(
218	    ["book", { __typename: "Book", pages: pages }],
219	    ["movie", { __typename: "Movie", minutes }],
220	    [@, null]
221	  )
222	  """)
223	}
224	```
225	
226	This works for `union Media = Book | Movie` and for `interface Media`. `pages`
227	and `minutes` read from the element the spread sits in, and `{ minutes }` is
228	the shorthand for `minutes: minutes`. An arm can also be written
229	`$ { __typename: $("Book") pages }`.
230	
231	What composition enforces, at `=2.15.2`:
232	
233	| Written | Result |
234	|---|---|
235	| a flat list, `id title pages minutes` | `SELECTED_FIELD_NOT_FOUND`: `minutes` does not exist on `Book` |
236	| `__typename: kind->match(["book", "Book"], …)` beside flat fields | the same. A `__typename` outside a spread narrows nothing |
237	| the shared fields only, `id title` | `CONNECTORS_UNRESOLVED_FIELD` for `Book.pages` and `Movie.minutes` |
238	| a member with no arm | `No matching shape found for selection. Attempted 1 different shape variations` |
239	| an arm with a field its member lacks | the same message |
240	| an arm with no `__typename`, one that names a non-member, or one computed (`__typename: kind`) | `INTERNAL: An internal error has occurred` |
241	
242	A field outside the spread has to exist on every member.
243	
244	**Only at a connector's own return type.** A union or interface field inside
245	another type's selection (`payment { ... type->match(…) }` on
246	`Order.payment: PaymentMethod`) fails with `GROUP_SELECTION_IS_NOT_OBJECT`.
247	Give that field its own `@connect` on `Order`, keyed by `$this.id`, and put the
248	spread in it: `$.payment { ... type->match(…) }`. That costs one request per
249	parent. When nothing can re-fetch the value, it stays a documented JSON scalar
250	([schema-authoring.md](schema-authoring.md#the-opaque-json-policy)).
251	
252	**An unmatched discriminator is a silent `null`.** Executed through Router
253	2.17.0 with a `podcast` element the arms do not list:
254	
255	- with `[@, null]`, the element is `null` and `errors` is empty;
256	- with no catch-all, a union element is `null` too. An interface's result
257	  then depends on the query: `{ media { id title } }` returns the podcast,
258	  and adding `__typename` or a fragment turns it into `null`;
259	- in a `[Media!]` list, the whole list is `null`, reported only in
260	  `extensions.valueCompletion`;
261	- a catch-all into a member, `[@, { __typename: "Book", … }]`, labels the
262	  podcast a `Book`, with `pages: null`.
263	
264	Write `[@, null]`, keep the element type nullable, and give e2e one case per
265	member plus one with a discriminator value the arms do not list.
266	
267	**Without a discriminator**, match on a key only some members send, through a
268	fallback: `... $(radius ?? "none")->match(["none", { __typename: "Rect", width,
269	height }], [@, { __typename: "Circle", radius }])`. The method does not run on
270	a missing key, so `radius->match([null, …], …)` yields `null` for every
271	`Rect`.
272	
273	**At v0.3** a union or interface is `CONNECTORS_UNSUPPORTED_ABSTRACT_TYPE`,
274	and `...` fails with "Spread syntax (...) is not supported in connect/v0.3
275	(use connect/v0.4)". A
276	polymorphic payload is a documented JSON scalar there.
277	
278	**What the skill's tools see**. `rover connector test` asserts a
279	spread correctly, and an unmatched element fails the case with
280	`Method ->match did not match any [candidate, value] pair`. The factory
281	readers parse this form, with each arm reading from the object the spread
282	sits in:
283	- `source-coverage` maps the discriminator and every arm's fields;
284	- `reconcile` reports an excluded field an arm maps;
285	- lint's `wire-enum-drift` and `int-overflow` check an arm's leaves against
286	  its `__typename` member. The source property comes from the `oneOf` variant
287	  whose discriminator `enum` holds the arm's candidate, so a `@` arm is not
288	  checked;
289	- `scaffold` asks for `__typename` and one `... on Member { … }` fragment per
290	  arm, with the fields beside the spread repeated in each.
291	
292	Any other spread (`... $.x { … }`, `... ->echo(…)`, a `->match` arm that is
293	neither an object nor `null`) reads `unresolved` in `source-coverage`,
294	naming the spread, for every path under that object the selection does not
295	otherwise map.
296	
297	## Literals
298	
299	At v0.4 the right-hand side of an alias is any expression, so a literal can be
300	written bare:
301	
302	```graphql
303	kind: "Book"            # "Book"
304	five: 5                 # 5
305	flag: true              # true
306	none: null              # null
307	fb: $.missing ?? "x"    # "x"
308	```
309	
310	`$( … )` still works and still means "this is a literal expression", and
311	`$."…"` reads a property whose name needs quoting. Both are unambiguous at
312	every version, so prefer them in anything that has to survive a move between
313	versions. The skill's own tools need them too: `graphos-factory-core reconcile`
314	reads a bare `true`, `false` or `null` as a property path ("the connector
315	selects … true"), and `$(true)` as a literal.
316	
317	**At v0.3 the same text means something else, silently.** A quoted string on
318	the right of an alias is a property **name**, and so are `true`, `false` and
319	`null`. Executed against `{"Book": "…", "true": "…", "false": "…", "null": "…"}`:
320	
321	| Selection | v0.3 | v0.4 |
322	|---|---|---|
323	| `looksLiteral: "Book"` | the `Book` property | `"Book"` |
324	| `bool: true` | the `true` property | `true` |
325	| `no: false` | the `false` property | `false` |
326	| `nul: null` | the `null` property | `null` |
327	| `properLiteral: $("Book")` | `"Book"` | `"Book"` |
328	| `propertyForm: $."Book"` | the `Book` property | the `Book` property |
329	
330	Neither version errors, so moving a schema from v0.3 to v0.4 can change what
331	it returns; [`connect-migrate`](#moving-a-workspace-from-v03-to-v04) finds such
332	sites in `selection`, and the other mapping arguments are checked by hand. At
333	v0.3 a bare number (`a: 5`) or an unwrapped operator chain (`a: $.x ?? "d"`)
334	does not parse; wrap it in `$( )`.
335	
336	## Variables
337	
338	| Variable | Bound to | Where |
339	|---|---|---|
340	| `$` | the value the enclosing `{ … }` received, or the response root | `selection`, `errors` |
341	| `@` | the value a method is operating on, rebound per element inside `->map` | method arguments |
342	| `$args` | the field's GraphQL arguments | root-field connectors |
343	| `$this` | the parent object, so sibling fields are reachable | non-root types |
344	| `$batch` | the collected keys | batch connectors |
345	| `$config` | values from router config | anywhere |
346	| `$env` | the router process environment | anywhere |
347	| `$context` | the router's request context, e.g. the caller's own credentials | anywhere |
348	| `$request.headers` | the client request's headers; each value is a list | anywhere |
349	| `$status` | the HTTP status | `selection`, `errors` |
350	| `$response.headers` | the API response's headers; each value is a list | `selection`, `errors` |
351	
352	`$` does **not** rebind inside a method argument, which is what makes
353	`$.first->and($.second)` work: `$.second` still reads from the enclosing
354	object, not from the result of `$.first`. Use `@` when you do want the value
355	flowing through the method.
356	
357	`rover connector test` injects `$args`, `$this`, `$batch`, `$config` and
358	`$context`, but **not** `$env`. `scripts/unit.sh` rewrites static
359	`{$env.NAME}` to `{$config.NAME}` in a temporary copy and the suites supply
360	`config.common.variables.$config`. Only a real router run proves `$env`.
361	
362	## Methods
363	
364	Written `value->method(args)`, chainable left to right, and always named here
365	with the leading `->`. The set is closed.
366	
367	### Which methods run
368	
369	The router that executes the connector decides which methods exist, not
370	the connect version. Routers 2.17 and 2.18 run the same **39 public
371	methods**, whatever the composition pin. `->withError` and `->withWarning`
372	are in no 2.x release up to 2.18.0, so do not use either. The connect
373	version decides how an existing method behaves: a breaking change to a
374	method applies only from the connect version that introduced it, so a
375	schema opts in by moving its link. `->typeof`, `->matchIf`,
376	`->has`, `->keys` and `->values` are not exposed at any release, so never reach
377	for them however they are documented elsewhere. An unavailable method is
378	neither a build error nor a runtime error: the field comes back `null`.
379	
380	### Picking things out of a list
381	
382	| Method | Does | Example |
383	|---|---|---|
384	| `->first` | first element | `colors->first` |
385	| `->last` | last element | `colors->last` |
386	| `->get(i)` | element at index; also a string char, or an object property by name | `items->get(2)`, `user->get("name")` |
387	| `->slice(a, b)` | sub-list, or substring | `colors->slice(0, 2)`, `$("abcdef")->slice(1, 3)` is `"bc"` |
388	| `->size` | list length, string length, or property count | `colors->size` |
389	| `->filter(cond)` | every element matching, `@` is the element | `users->filter(@.active->eq(true))` |
390	| `->find(cond)` | the first element matching, else nothing | `users->find(@.active->eq(true))` |
391	| `->map(expr)` | apply to each element; on a non-list, a one-element list (`27` gives `[54]`) | `numbers->map(@->mul(2))` |
392	| `->entries` | object to `[{key, value}, …]`; `->entries.key` for just the keys | `obj->entries` |
393	| `->joinNotNull(sep)` | joins a list of scalars, skipping nulls | `$(["a", null, "b"])->joinNotNull(",")` is `"a,b"` |
394	
395	### Comparing and testing
396	
397	`->eq` `->ne` `->gt` `->gte` `->lt` `->lte` compare against their argument and
398	return a boolean. `->in([…])` is true when the value is one of the listed
399	values; `->contains(v)` is true when the **list** it is applied to holds `v`.
400	Note the direction: `$(123)->in([123, 456])` and `$([123, 456])->contains(123)`
401	are the same question asked from opposite ends. `->and` `->or` take further
402	values, `->not` inverts.
403	
404	**Combining conditions inside `->filter` or `->find` needs `->as`.** `@` rebinds in
405	every method, so in `@.active->and(@.age->gt(30))` the inner `@` is the boolean
406	`@.active`, and the router returns `null` for the whole field with no error.
407	If the first condition is itself a method call (`@.a->eq("x")->and(…)`),
408	composition fails instead, with a misleading `CONNECTORS_UNRESOLVED_FIELD`
409	on every field of the type. Bind the element first:
410	
411	```graphql
412	adults: users->filter(@->as($u)->echo($u.active)->and($u.age->gt(30)))
413	```
414	
415	Use the `->as` form unless the router the service runs on is 2.18.0 or
416	later. Before 2.18.0, a `->filter` or `->find` after another list-producing
417	method, followed by a sub-selection
418	(`users->filter(@.active)->filter(@.age->gt(30)) { id name }`,
419	`users->filter(@.active)->find(@.age->gt(30)) { id name }`), composes, and
420	then the router will not start ("… all of its members are @inaccessible").
421	Without a sub-selection (`…->filter(…)->map(@.name)`) the chain works.
422	
423	### Strings
424	
425	| Method | Does | Example |
426	|---|---|---|
427	| `->split(sep)` | string to list | `$("a,b,c")->split(",")` is `["a","b","c"]` |
428	| `->trim`, `->trimStart`, `->trimEnd` | strip whitespace | `$("  hi  ")->trim` is `"hi"` |
429	
430	A comma-separated header or field becomes a clean list with
431	`tags->split(",")->map(@->trim)`.
432	
433	### Arithmetic and conversion
434	
435	`->add` `->sub` `->mul` `->div` `->mod` work on integers and floats.
436	`->toString` renders a scalar (`null` becomes `""`; a list or object is an
437	error). `->parseInt` takes an optional base, so `$("ff")->parseInt(16)` is
438	`255`. `->jsonStringify` serialises a value to a JSON string, and `->jsonParse`
439	reverses it:
440	`$('{"x":1}')->jsonParse` is `{x: 1}`, which unpacks an API that embeds JSON in
441	a string field.
442	
443	### The rest
444	
445	| Method | Does |
446	|---|---|
447	| `->echo(x)` | returns its argument, ignoring the input |
448	| `->as($var[, expr])` | returns the input unchanged **and** binds it (or `expr`) to `$var` for later in the chain: `person->as($n, @.name)->echo($n)` is `"Ben"` |
449	| `->match([a, x], [b, y], [@, z])` | value translation; a final `[@, …]` pair is the catch-all |
450	| `->keysToCamelCase`, `->keysToCamelCaseDeep` | see [Renaming snake_case keys in bulk](#renaming-snake_case-keys-in-bulk) |
451	
452	`->match` is how an enum crosses the wire boundary. Executed, with
453	`status: "open"`:
454	
455	```graphql
456	state: status->match(['open', 'OPEN'], ['closed', 'CLOSED'], [@, 'UNKNOWN'])
457	```
458	
459	gives `"OPEN"`, and an unlisted input gives `"UNKNOWN"`. Without the `[@, …]`
460	catch-all an unmatched value drops the output key, and the router returns
461	`null` with no error.
462	[naming.md](naming.md) explains when to translate and when to keep the wire
463	casing instead; `graphos-factory-core lint` checks the two agree
464	(`wire-enum-drift`).
465	
466	## Absence: `?.`, `?->`, `??`, `?!`
467	
468	These read like JavaScript's optional chaining and nullish coalescing, and
469	mostly behave like them. Executed through Router 2.17 against
470	`{"person": {"name": "Ben"}, "size": null, "n": 27}`:
471	
472	| Selection | Result | JavaScript counterpart |
473	|---|---|---|
474	| `$.nobody?.absent` | `null` | `nobody?.absent` |
475	| `size?->jsonStringify` | `null` | `size?.jsonStringify()` |
476	| `size->jsonStringify` | `"null"` | none: the method runs on `null` |
477	| `n?->jsonStringify` | `"27"` | `n?.jsonStringify()` |
478	| `$.nobody.absent ?? "fb"` | `"fb"` | `nobody?.absent ?? "fb"` |
479	| `$.size ?! "fb"` | `null` | `size === undefined ? "fb" : size` |
480	
481	Where they differ from JavaScript:
482	
483	- **A missing step is never an exception.** `$.nobody.absent` is `null` with or
484	  without the `?`, where JavaScript's `nobody.absent` would throw. On a path,
485	  `?` marks the step you expect may be missing; it does not change the result.
486	- **`?->` is where `?` matters.** A method runs on `null` unless the step before
487	  it is guarded: `size->jsonStringify` turns a JSON `null` into the four-character
488	  string `"null"`, and `size?->jsonStringify` keeps it `null`.
489	- **A `?` can close a path.** `$.person.absent?` has no JavaScript form; it marks
490	  the last step as optional.
491	- **"Missing" is JavaScript's `undefined`.** `??` falls back when the value is
492	  `null` or missing, as in JavaScript. `?!` falls back only when it is missing,
493	  so an explicit `null` from the API survives. Use `??` for an error-message
494	  fallback, where anything beats empty, and `?!` when the API distinguishes
495	  "not set" from "set to null" and the schema should too.
496	- **Operators cannot be mixed in one chain.** `a ?? b ?? c` is fine;
497	  `a ?? b ?! c` does not compose.
498	
499	A key that the selection drops and a key the API sent as `null` look the same
500	to the client: a nullable field reads `null`, and a non-null field nulls its
501	parent object.
502	
503	**At v0.3** an operator chain has to be wrapped: `nn: $($.nullField ?? 'fallback')`.
504	The wrapped form works at both versions.
505	
506	## Building requests
507	
508	`queryParams` and `body` use the same language as `selection`; a header value
509	is a string template, and only its `{…}` expressions do. An entry whose value
510	is null is omitted from the request, which is how an optional argument stays
511	optional:
512	
513	```graphql
514	http: {
515	  GET: "/widgets"
516	  queryParams: """
517	  limit: $args.limit
518	  cursor: $args.cursor
519	  """
520	}
521	```
522	
523	A request body is a literal object. Keys are the API's wire names, not the
524	GraphQL ones, and a literal value can sit beside the arguments:
525	
526	```graphql
527	body: """
528	{
529	  channel: $args.channel,
530	  thread_ts: $args.threadTs,
531	  kind: "message"
532	}
533	"""
534	```
535	
536	Executed with `channel: "C1"`, `threadTs: "123.4"`, that sends
537	`{"channel":"C1","thread_ts":"123.4","kind":"message"}`. A body written as
538	plain mapping lines (`channel: $args.channel` on its own) also works.
539	
540	Inside the braces, separate the entries with commas. The skill's tools read a
541	braced body as comma-separated: on gitea's issue-create body, dropping the
542	commas takes `source-coverage` from 8 request fields mapped to 0.
543	
544	**At v0.3** the braces must be wrapped, `body: "$({ a: $args.a })"`; the
545	wrapped form is valid at both versions.
546	
547	## Moving a workspace from v0.3 to v0.4
548	
549	Use [`connect-migrate`](https://github.com/apollographql/connect-migrate). It
550	parses every `@connect(selection: …)` with the real Connectors parser at both
551	the schema's linked version and v0.4, and lists the sites whose meaning would
552	change ([Literals](#literals)) with the rewrite that preserves each one.
553	
554	1. **Install it.** `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apollographql/connect-migrate/main/install.sh | sh`
555	   puts `connect-migrate` in `~/.local/bin`. The binaries are unsigned; where
556	   that is a problem, build it from the router repository instead:
557	   `cargo build --release --bin connect-migrate --features connect-migrate` in
558	   `apollo-federation/`.
559	2. **Follow its guide.** `connect-migrate agent-guide` prints the procedure.
560	   In short: `connect-migrate analyze <workspace> -o manifest.md`; apply the
561	   manifest's rewrites; put only its questions to the user; run `analyze`
562	   again **while the schema still links v0.3** until it reports nothing to
563	   change; bump the `@link` last, after step 3.
564	3. **Check the rest by hand.** `connect-migrate` reads only `selection`, but
565	   `body`, `queryParams`, `path`, `isSuccess` and `errors`, on `@connect` and
566	   on `@source`, are parsed at the linked version too. In each, find every
567	   quoted string, `true`, `false` or `null` after an alias, and rewrite it as
568	   `$."…"` to keep the v0.3 property read, or as `$( … )` if the literal was
569	   meant. Leave `headers` out: a header value is a string template, not a
570	   mapping.
571	4. **Move the workspace pins with it.** Set `connect_spec: v0.4` and
572	   `federation_version: "2.15.2"` in `.factory/workspace.yaml`, and `=2.15.2`
573	   in `supergraph.yaml`. The `federation/` link can move or stay: lint's
574	   `federation-drift` checks it against `federation_spec_version` when that is
575	   set, and against `federation_version` when it is not. To move it, link
576	   `federation/v2.15` and delete `federation_spec_version`, which is only for a
577	   link that differs from the plugin pin ([workspace-contract.md](workspace-contract.md)),
578	   or set it to `"2.15"`. To keep it, set `federation_spec_version` to the
579	   version it links, as the pilots do (`federation/v2.12`,
580	   `"2.12"`). `graphos-factory-core lint` and `render` fail until the pins and the
581	   schema agree.
582	5. **Treat the rewrites as schema edits.** Record them under SKILL.md's
583	   hand-edit policy, record the move with `graphos-factory-core decisions`, then
584	   compose and run the e2e layer.
585	
586	## Troubleshooting
587	
588	**A field is `null` and the response has no error.** The router reports
589	mapping problems this way: an unavailable method, a `->match` with no `[@, …]`
590	catch-all, `->and` inside `->filter`, a missing property, a non-null field left
591	empty. Check the selection against the payload, and assert the values you care
592	about in the e2e suite, which serves the schema through a real router. Results
593	from `rover connector test` are not evidence of what the router does.
594	
595	**Every response-derived field is `null`, but literals and `$args` come
596	through.** The API or stub is answering without a JSON content type
597	(`application/octet-stream`, `text/plain`). Check the `Content-Type` before
598	debugging the selection.
599	
600	**`GROUP_SELECTION_IS_NOT_OBJECT`.** A `{ … }` group, or a method whose result
601	composition can see is an object list (`raw: $.obj->entries`), targets a
602	`JSON`-typed field. Type the object. On a union or interface field, see
603	[Abstract types](#abstract-types).
604	
605	**`INTERNAL` or `No matching shape found for selection` on a union or
606	interface.** An arm lacks a literal `__typename`, names a non-member, selects
607	a field its member lacks, or a member has no arm
608	([Abstract types](#abstract-types)).
609	
610	## Appendix: the grammar at `connect/v0.4`
611	
612	Extended Backus-Naur Form, as implemented at `federation_version: =2.15.2`.
613	Whitespace and `#` comments are allowed between any two tokens **except**
614	where `NO_SPACE` forbids it, which is why `$ args` and a broken-up identifier
615	are invalid.
616	
617	```ebnf
618	JSONSelection        ::= LitExpr | NamedSelectionList
619	NamedSelectionList   ::= NamedSelection ("," NamedSelection)* ","? | NamedSelection*
620	SubSelection         ::= "{" NamedSelectionList "}"
621	NamedSelection       ::= "..." LitExpr
622	                       | Alias LitExpr
623	                       | PathSelection
624	Alias                ::= Key ":"
625	PathSelection        ::= (VarPath | KeyPath | AtPath | ExprPath) SubSelection?
626	VarPath              ::= "$" (NO_SPACE Identifier)? PathTail
627	KeyPath              ::= Key PathTail
628	AtPath               ::= "@" PathTail
629	ExprPath             ::= "$(" LitExpr ")" PathTail
630	PathTail             ::= "?"? (PathStep "?"?)*
631	NonEmptyPathTail     ::= "?"? (PathStep "?"?)+ | "?"
632	PathStep             ::= "." Key | "->" Identifier MethodArgs?
633	Key                  ::= Identifier | LitString
634	Identifier           ::= [a-zA-Z_] NO_SPACE [0-9a-zA-Z_]*
635	MethodArgs           ::= "(" (LitExpr ("," LitExpr)* ","?)? ")"
636	LitExpr              ::= LitOpChain | LitPath | LitPrimitive | LitObject | LitArray | PathSelection
637	LitOpChain           ::= LitExpr (LitOp LitExpr)+
638	LitOp                ::= "??" | "?!"
639	LitPath              ::= (LitPrimitive | LitObject | LitArray) NonEmptyPathTail
640	LitPrimitive         ::= LitString | LitNumber | "true" | "false" | "null"
641	LitString            ::= "'" ("\\'" | [^'])* "'" | '"' ('\\"' | [^"])* '"'
642	LitNumber            ::= "-"? ([0-9]+ ("." [0-9]*)? | "." [0-9]+)
643	LitObject            ::= SubSelection
644	LitArray             ::= "[" (LitExpr ("," LitExpr)* ","?)? "]"
645	NO_SPACE             ::= !SpacesOrComments
646	SpacesOrComments     ::= (Spaces | Comment)+
647	Spaces               ::= (" " | "\t" | "\r" | "\n")+
648	Comment              ::= "#" [^\n]*
649	```
650	
651	What the prose above depends on:
652	
653	- **`NamedSelectionList`** is either comma-separated or whitespace-separated,
654	  never mixed. That is [Separators](#separators).
655	- **`Alias LitExpr`** is why a literal can follow an alias
656	  ([Literals](#literals)).
657	- **A `PathSelection` contributes its key only when the path is one key long.**
658	  That is the single-key rule.
659	
660	### What v0.3 lacks
661	
662	The v0.3 grammar is this one with four differences:
663	
664	```ebnf
665	JSONSelection        ::= NamedSelection*
666	SubSelection         ::= "{" NamedSelection* "}"
667	NamedSelection       ::= (Alias | "...")? PathSelection | Alias SubSelection
668	LitObject            ::= "{" (LitProperty ("," LitProperty)* ","?)? "}"
669	LitProperty          ::= Key ":" LitExpr
670	```
671	
672	No commas in a selection list; an alias takes only a path or a sub-selection,
673	never a literal (which is why `a: "Book"` reads a property there); `...` is
674	rejected outright despite the grammar's `"..."`; and a literal object is its
675	own rule, reachable only inside `$( )`.
676	
677	## Appendix: reproducing these measurements
678	
679	Everything version-dependent here is a measurement. Two instruments did the
680	measuring:
681	
682	- **Composition** (`rover supergraph compose` at the pin) decides what parses
683	  and what builds: the pin and link tables, the grammar, and the build error in
684	  [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).
685	- **The router** decides what a selection produces. Every runtime result in
686	  this file was read from Apollo Router 2.17.0 serving the composed supergraph
687	  against local stubs: a static JSON file per connector, served as
688	  `application/json`, and an echo server for request bodies.
689	
690	To re-measure after changing `federation_version`, `connect_spec` or the router
691	version: write a schema that uses each form once, compose it, check that the
692	compose succeeded, and query it through the router, or run the workspace's e2e
693	layer, which does the same with WireMock.
694	
695	Composition was measured with rover 0.41.0 at federation 2.12.0, 2.13.0,
696	2.14.0, 2.14.3, 2.15.0 and 2.15.2, at both connect spec versions, and at
697	2.15.1 for the grammar note under the pin table. Runtime results come from
698	Router 2.17.0 on schemas composed at 2.15.2 (`connect/v0.4`) and 2.12.0
699	(`connect/v0.3`). [Abstract types](#abstract-types) was measured the same way:
700	composition at 2.15.2 and at 2.12.0, and runtime on Router 2.17.0.
701	
702	Every selection and every result in this file was produced that way. If you
703	change one, re-run it.

1	# Naming
2	
3	Every name in a connector schema shares one namespace with every other
4	subgraph in the supergraph. The prefixes are what keep two connectors from
5	colliding, and they are mechanical — `graphos-factory-core lint` checks all of them.
6	
7	## The four names of one service
8	
9	For a service whose directory is `widget-co`:
10	
11	| Name | Value | Where it appears |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| directory / subgraph | `widget-co` | directory, `supergraph.yaml` key, schema filename |
14	| source / service | `widget_co` | `@source(name:)`, `workspace.yaml` `service` |
15	| type prefix | `Widget_Co` | `type Widget_Co_Widget` |
16	| field prefix | `widget_co` | `Query.widget_co_listWidgets` |
17	
18	**The other three derive from the directory.** Snake-case the directory
19	for the source and field prefix, and capitalise each part for the type
20	prefix: `widget-co` gives `widget_co`, `Widget_Co_` and `widget_co_`. The
21	table above follows that rule. A vendor's own casing (`GitHub_`, not
22	`Github_`) or a short source name (`gsc` for `google-search-console`) is
23	allowed; a target that derives the names itself says what it needs to
24	accept a different one.
25	
26	**The directory may be snake_case** (`widget_co`) when a consumer needs
27	the schema file under that name — the AppWorld benchmark bundle reads
28	`<app>.graphql`, so `simple_note` rather than `simple-note`. The schema
29	filename is always `<directory>.graphql`. `workspace.yaml`'s `directory`
30	accepts kebab- or snake-case words (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`), and the choice
31	changes nothing else: the rule snake-cases either form first, so
32	`widget_co` still derives `widget_co`, `Widget_Co_` and `widget_co_`, and
33	rover gives the same `WIDGET_CO`. A snake_case directory is not a licence
34	for a CamelCase type prefix.
35	
36	**Multi-word names use snake_case, never camelCase.** `rover supergraph
37	compose` derives the `join__Graph` enum value from the subgraph name by
38	uppercasing and replacing hyphens with underscores — `widget-co` →
39	`WIDGET_CO`. `@source(name: "widgetCo")` still composes; it just leaves the
40	subgraph schema and the composed supergraph SDL disagreeing about the
41	service's name, in a way that is easy to miss in review and annoying to
42	unpick later.
43	
44	## Types and fields
45	
46	```graphql
47	type Widget_Co_Widget { ... }          # {TypePrefix}_{TypeName}, PascalCase after the prefix
48	scalar Widget_Co_JSON                  # the one opaque scalar, if any
49	enum Widget_Co_WidgetStatus { ... }
50	
51	type Query {
52	  widget_co_listWidgets(...): [Widget_Co_Widget]   # {field_prefix}_{camelCase}
53	}
54	```
55	
56	`Query`, `Mutation` and `Subscription` are the federation roots and are
57	never prefixed. Everything else is.
58	
59	Nested types take the path that produced them, so the name says where it
60	came from: `Widget_Co_Widget_Owner`, not `Widget_Co_Owner2`. If two paths
61	genuinely produce the same shape, share one type and record that as a
62	decision in `decisions.json`.
63	
64	An inline (non-`$ref`) request body becomes an input type named after the
65	operation's `graphql.name` — `{TypePrefix}_{OpName}Input`
66	(`Widget_Co_CreateWidgetInput`), never a placeholder (`Input`, `Input2`) — and
67	an inline array body's item type is `{TypePrefix}_{OpName}ItemInput`. A `$ref`
68	body keeps its component name.
69	
70	## Field naming inside the selection
71	
72	REST payloads are usually `snake_case`; GraphQL fields are `camelCase`. Do
73	the rename in the `@connect` selection, not by renaming the API's fields in
74	your head:
75	
76	```graphql
77	selection: """
78	channelId: channel_id
79	postAt: post_at
80	nextCursor: response_metadata.next_cursor
81	"""
82	```
83	
84	Two exceptions worth taking deliberately:
85	
86	- **Keep the vendor's casing when it is the API's own vocabulary** — an
87	  enum whose values serialise straight back into a request body should keep
88	  the wire casing rather than gain a `->match` translation table in both
89	  directions. This rule settles it, so following it is not a decision:
90	  record it as a finding (`graphos-factory-core findings add --cites
91	  references/naming.md`) only when an instrument needs it, keep a decision
92	  in `decisions.json` for a departure from it, and apply it to the
93	  whole connector. `graphos-factory-core lint` checks the other direction
94	  (`wire-enum-drift`): an enum value the spec does not list for the
95	  parameter or property it maps to, or a listed value the enum lacks, is a
96	  warning unless the connector translates it with `->match`. The converse is
97	  checked too (`closed-enum-as-string`): a `String` argument or
98	  field over a spec vocabulary of two or more values, every one a valid
99	  GraphQL name — declared at every spec property a selected operation
100	  reaches the field through — is a warning until it is an enum in wire
101	  casing or a resolved decision names the slot in `affects`.
102	- **Keep a name that is already `camelCase` on the wire.** Renaming for
103	  symmetry costs a mapping and buys nothing.
104	
105	A snake_case field on a prefixed type, or a root field whose name after the
106	prefix is snake_case, is a lint warning (`field-casing`); a doc comment on
107	the field saying why the wire name is kept is the recorded exception.
108	
109	## Operation names and the semantic root
110	
111	The field name comes from `selection.yaml`'s `graphql.name`, unprefixed;
112	the prefix is added on emit. Prefer the name a user of the API would use
113	(`listWidgets`, `widget`, `createWidget`) over the vendor's `operationId`,
114	which is frequently copy-pasted from a sibling endpoint and wrong.
115	
116	**Query vs Mutation is semantic and is never derived from the HTTP method.**
117	A POST that searches is a `Query`; a GET that mints a token is a `Mutation`.
118	This matters beyond taste: a POST is a write until the user says so. The
119	inventory records every POST as `semantics: write`, because a write
120	mistaken for a read puts a side effect under `Query`, where callers,
121	caches and retries treat it as safe, while a read mistaken for a write only
122	changes the schema's root. A POST whose name carries a read verb (`renderMarkdown`,
123	`/schedules/preview`, `repoGetFileContentsPost`) carries a `read_hint`, and
124	`inventory list` marks it `[read?]`. Surface every hinted POST to the user
125	and ask which are reads **before** writing `root: query` for any of them;
126	`selection.yaml` must carry an explicit `graphql.root`, `graphos-factory-core
127	lint` fails when it does not, and `read-root-on-write` warns on every POST
128	selected as a `Query` until `decisions.json` records why.
129	
130	## Renames and collisions
131	
132	- Two operations may not map to the same field name — lint catches it.
133	- Within one type, two source fields may not rename to the same GraphQL
134	  name.
135	- When the API has an `id`-like field, expose it as `ID`, not `String`,
136	  and use it as the `@key` if the type becomes an entity.

1	# The Apollo Connectors language
2	
3	What `@source` and `@connect` can express, and the shapes that recur in every
4	connector. The mapping language that goes *inside* them (`selection`, `body`,
5	`queryParams`, the methods, the null operators) is
6	[mapping-language.md](mapping-language.md).
7	
8	The hosted GraphOS MCP server's `ApolloConnectorsSpec` tool has worked
9	examples worth reading, but it is written for `connect/v0.3` and
10	federation 2.12. Some of its rules (every literal needs `$( )`, a bare-brace
11	body does not compose) hold only at v0.3, and its `rover connector run` step
12	is not evidence ([testing.md](testing.md)). Where it disagrees with this
13	file, this file wins.
14	
15	## Linking the spec
16	
17	```graphql
18	extend schema
19	  @link(url: "https://specs.apollo.dev/federation/v2.15", import: ["@key", "@shareable", "@tag"])
20	  @link(url: "https://specs.apollo.dev/connect/v0.4", import: ["@source", "@connect"])
21	```
22	
23	That is the target: `connect/v0.4`, composed at `federation_version: =2.15.2`,
24	served by Apollo Router 2.17. Since Router 2.18.0, v0.4 is no longer a
25	preview version (Router 2.16.0 and later need no opt-in for it). Never link `connect/v0.5` unless the user asks for it
26	([v0.5](#v05-preview-do-not-link)). A workspace created before the move may still
27	link `federation/v2.12` and `connect/v0.3` at `federation_version: =2.12.0`
28	until someone moves the pin
29	([mapping-language.md](mapping-language.md#moving-a-workspace-from-v03-to-v04)),
30	and a workspace can keep an older `federation/` link than its pin by recording
31	it as `federation_spec_version`.
32	
33	The connect version and the federation version are both pinned in
34	`.factory/workspace.yaml`; `graphos-factory-core lint` fails when the schema drifts
35	from either pin, and `graphos-factory-core render` fails when `supergraph.yaml` and
36	`workspace.yaml` disagree. The `federation/` link can be no newer than
37	`federation_version`, and a newer one fails composition in one of two ways: at
38	2.12.0, `INTERNAL_ERROR` with `Unexpected federation version: 2.15`; at
39	2.14.0, `Unknown directive "@source"`, naming the connect directive when the
40	fault is the federation link. The same `Unknown directive "@source"` appears
41	at 2.12.0 with `federation/v2.12` and `connect/v0.4`, where the connect link is
42	the cause. A federation pin is part of the test, not incidental: the same
43	schema can compose at 2.12 and fail at 2.15 with a named build error the older
44	composer masked. Quote the pin whenever you
45	quote a compose result.
46	
47	## `@source`
48	
49	One per schema. The core's layers render one `@source`, and a target may
50	make that a hard limit for its deployment (its contract reference says
51	why), so treat it as one, not a style preference.
52	
53	```graphql
54	@source(
55	  name: "widget_co"
56	  http: {
57	    baseURL: "{{BASE_URL}}"
58	    headers: [
59	      { name: "Authorization", value: "Bearer {{AUTH_EXPR}}" }
60	      { name: "User-Agent", value: "widget-co-connector" }
61	    ]
62	  }
63	  errors: {
64	    message: "$($.error.message ?? 'Widget Co request failed')"
65	    extensions: """
66	    httpStatus: $status
67	    """
68	  }
69	)
70	```
71	
72	`errors` maps a non-2xx body into the GraphQL error. The path above
73	(`$.error.message`) is this one API's documented error body, not a
74	template — take the actual path from what the API's spec documents for
75	its error responses, never copy a path from another connector or from a
76	different API's convention (`.detail` is FastAPI's default; plenty of APIs
77	use it, plenty don't). [schema-authoring.md § Errors](schema-authoring.md#errors)
78	says how: read the selected operations' `errors[]` in
79	`.factory/inventory.json`, follow each `shape_ref` into `shapes`, and write
80	the path that shape actually carries. Give the message expression a `??`
81	fallback: most APIs document a JSON error body for some statuses and
82	nothing at all for others (401, 408, 429 are the usual bare ones), and
83	without a fallback those produce an empty message.
84	
85	## `@connect`
86	
87	On a root field:
88	
89	```graphql
90	type Query {
91	  widget_co_listWidgets(limit: Int, cursor: String): Widget_Co_WidgetList
92	    @connect(
93	      source: "widget_co"
94	      http: {
95	        GET: "/widgets"
96	        queryParams: """
97	        limit: $args.limit
98	        cursor: $args.cursor
99	        """
100	      }
101	      selection: """
102	      widgets {
103	        id
104	        createdAt: created_at
105	      }
106	      nextCursor: page_info.next_cursor
107	      """
108	    )
109	}
110	```
111	
112	- **Methods**: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, each taking the URI
113	  template as its value. Path variables interpolate expressions:
114	  `GET: "/widgets/{$args.id}"`.
115	- **`queryParams`** is mapping entries separated by whitespace, not GraphQL
116	  — one per line in every pilot, and several on one line
117	  (`a: $args.a b: $args.b`) is the same block to the router and
118	  to the lint rules and `scaffold` that read it. A null-valued
119	  entry is omitted from the request.
120	- **`headers`** is a GraphQL list of `{ name, value }` objects, the form the
121	  `@source` example above uses; a value may interpolate an expression
122	  (`headers: [{ name: "From", value: "{$args.from}" }]`).
123	- **`body`** builds the request payload, usually a literal object whose keys
124	  are the API's wire names:
125	
126	  ```graphql
127	  body: """
128	  {
129	    channel: $args.channel,
130	    text: $args.text,
131	    thread_ts: $args.threadTs
132	  }
133	  """
134	  ```
135	
136	  At v0.3 the braces must be wrapped as `$({ … })`; the wrapped form is valid
137	  at both versions.
138	
139	  **A null argument is sent, not dropped, unless the member guards it.** An
140	  argument left out leaves its key out; an explicit `null` is sent as JSON
141	  `null` (`title: $args.title`) or, through `->map({ id: @ })->first`, as
142	  `{id: null}` (measured on the router, pagerduty and gitea). `$args.x?`
143	  drops the key when the value is null or absent and nothing else: an empty
144	  string, an empty list, `false` and `0` go through, and a null nested inside
145	  an object the argument keeps stays. Write `$args.x?->map(…)->first` to drop
146	  a wrapped member on a null too. Use it where the source description does
147	  not allow a null at that key.
148	
149	- **`selection`** maps the response into the field's type. It is a shape,
150	  not a query: `alias: source_path` renames, nesting descends, and a field
151	  named identically on both sides is written once. Every field of the
152	  return type must be reachable in the selection or compose fails.
153	- **A method on a leaf must be aliased.** `size: size->jsonStringify` maps a
154	  64-bit number onto a `String` field and composes; the bare
155	  `size->jsonStringify` is rejected with `INVALID_SELECTION: SubSelection
156	  cannot contain multiple elements if it contains an anonymous
157	  NamedSelection` (rover 0.41.0, connect v0.3) — the name a method produces
158	  is anonymous, so the selection has to give it one. It applies to every
159	  method, and to a subselection too: deck-of-cards writes
160	  `piles: piles->entries { … }`, never `piles->entries { … }`. A method inside
161	  `queryParams` or `body` is a different position and needs no alias
162	  (`cards: $args.cards->joinNotNull(",")` is the entry's own key).
163	- **A method does not skip a `null`; `?->` and `->match` do.**
164	  `size->jsonStringify` on a JSON `null` produces the four-character string
165	  `"null"`, not `null`. Every form, run through Apollo Router 2.17 with a
166	  `{ "size": null }` body (the same at connect v0.3 and v0.4):
167	
168	  | Written | null body | `27` body |
169	  |---|---|---|
170	  | `size->jsonStringify` | `"null"` | `"27"` |
171	  | `size?->jsonStringify` | key omitted from the mapped object | `"27"` |
172	  | `$(size?->jsonStringify ?? null)` | `null` | `"27"` |
173	  | `size->match([null, null], [@, @->jsonStringify])` | `null` | `"27"` |
174	
175	  Both null-preserving forms resolve their path **relative to the enclosing
176	  subselection**, not to the response root. Prefer the `->match` form:
177	  `reconcile` reads `alias: path->method(…)` as a mapping of `path`, but does
178	  not read a `$(…)` expression block that way, so a `$(…)`-wrapped leaf is
179	  reported as `renamed by the selection but the connector does not map it`
180	  and counted in `selection says all fields; N not mapped`.
181	
182	## Expression variables
183	
184	| Variable | Available in | Notes |
185	|---|---|---|
186	| `$args` | root-field connectors, and a field-level connector's own declared arguments | the field's arguments; a relationship field (§ Relationship fields) declares only the per-call credential argument its by-id root field declares, and none under source-level auth |
187	| `$this` | connectors on a non-root type | the parent object, so sibling fields are reachable; for an entity, the key fields it references become the key |
188	| `$batch` | batch connectors | the collected keys |
189	| `$config` | anywhere | values the router config supplies |
190	| `$env` | anywhere | process environment |
191	| `$context` | anywhere | request context, e.g. the caller's own credentials |
192	| `$status`, `$` | `selection`, and `errors` on `@connect` or `@source` | HTTP status and the response body |
193	
194	`rover connector test` injects `$args`, `$this`, `$batch`, `$config` and
195	`$context` — but **not** `$env`. That is why `scripts/unit.sh` rewrites
196	static `{$env.NAME}` to `{$config.NAME}` in a temporary copy of the schema
197	and the suites supply `config.common.variables.$config` (`unit.sh` fails,
198	before rover runs, a suite with cases that lacks one, naming it). Exporting the
199	variable into rover's process does not help. Only a real router run proves
200	`$env` or `$context` injection.
201	
202	## Entities
203	
204	A type-level `@connect` plus `@key` makes a type resolvable on its own, so
205	another subgraph can reference it:
206	
207	```graphql
208	type Widget_Co_Widget
209	  @key(fields: "id")
210	  @connect(
211	    source: "widget_co"
212	    http: { GET: "/widgets/{$this.id}" }
213	    selection: "id name"
214	  ) {
215	  id: ID!
216	  name: String
217	}
218	```
219	
220	`@key` is what makes the type an entity. **The connector's own key is derived
221	from the variables it references** (`Connector::resolvable_key`): `$this` for
222	a field-level or type-level connector, `$batch` for a batch one, `$args` for
223	`@connect(entity: true)` on a `Query` field. That derived key decides which
224	`@key` the connector can resolve, not whether the federation key exists. The
225	example's connector resolves `id` because the URI interpolates `$this.id`.
226	
227	Validation runs in one direction only, which is what makes this worth knowing:
228	
229	- A hand-written `@key` that **no** connector can resolve fails loudly, with
230	  `MISSING_ENTITY_CONNECTOR`. Writing `@key` commits you to resolving it.
231	- A type-level `@connect` **without** `@key` is silent. It composes to a
232	  keyless type no other subgraph can reference (one that tries fails with
233	  `INVALID_FIELD_SHARING`): it looks like it worked and buys nothing.
234	
235	Lint checks every `@key` type: it needs a lookup by each
236	resolvable key, one full key wherever a connector's selection embeds it,
237	something that returns it, and a connector mapping each of its fields. A
238	`@key(fields: "id", resolvable: false)` stub, which references another
239	subgraph's entity, needs no lookup and no field connectors. The embedding is
240	read through the selection, so `pet { id: pet_id }` carries `id`.
241	
242	Only make a type an entity when a decision records why in `decisions.json`
243	(`graphos-factory-core decisions`); entities widen the supergraph's contract.
244	
245	These rules assume this subgraph owns the entity. A type another subgraph
246	owns is declared under its owner's exact name only when a resolved decision
247	records it (`decisions add --foreign-type NAME`), and only a target that
248	allows it reads that record. There, the declared type is exempt from the
249	prefix rule, and from the lookup rule when every connector on it is
250	field-level and reads `$this`; the target's own reference says what it
251	checks instead. Under a target that does not read the record, every type
252	keeps the prefix and every rule above.
253	
254	### At v0.4, a `Query` connector can hijack entity resolution
255	
256	Suppose an entity has a type-level `@connect` that resolves it from `$this`
257	or `$batch`,
258	and a `Query` field `@connect` (mapping from `$args`, without
259	`entity: true`) also returns that type. At v0.4 the router may resolve
260	references to the entity through the `Query` connector. `$args` is empty
261	there, so the request goes out without its parameters and fails, usually as
262	a `400` reported as `CONNECTOR_FETCH`. v0.3 does not do this, so changing
263	only the `@link` to v0.4 can break a schema that worked.
264	
265	The fix ([router#9853](https://github.com/apollographql/router/pull/9853))
266	is not in a release yet; Router 2.18.0 does not have it. Whether a given
267	schema misroutes is up to the query planner, so a passing run does not
268	prove it is safe. An e2e case whose stub for the entity's own connector is
269	`x-required` catches it ([testing.md](testing.md)).
270	[Finding a `$batch` candidate](#finding-a-batch-candidate) has a case where
271	it happened.
272	
273	## Relationship fields
274	
275	A response property that carries another resource's id (`album_id` on a
276	song, `owner_id` on a widget) becomes a field on the type that carries it,
277	resolved by that resource's GET-by-id operation through a **field-level**
278	connector keyed by `$this`:
279	
280	```graphql
281	type Widget_Co_Widget {
282	  id: ID!
283	  owner_id: ID
284	  """
285	  The Widget_Co_Owner referenced by `owner_id`, fetched by the router through get:/owners/{ownerId}, one request per Widget_Co_Widget that selects it; select this instead of calling Query.widget_co_owner per item.
286	  """
287	  owner: Widget_Co_Owner
288	    @connect(
289	      source: "widget_co"
290	      http: { GET: "/owners/{$this.owner_id}" }
291	      isSuccess: "$($this.owner_id ?! 0)->match([null, true], [@, $status->gte(200)->and($status->lt(300))])"
292	      selection: """
293	      $($this.owner_id ?! 0)->match([null, null], [@, $ {
294	        id login
295	      }])
296	      """
297	    )
298	}
299	```
300	
301	(`owner_id` is nullable, so the field carries the null guard below; with
302	`owner_id: ID!` it is the plain `selection: """id login"""` and no
303	`isSuccess`.)
304	
305	What it is and is not:
306	
307	- **No `@key`, no `entity: true`, no type-level `@connect`.** The field is
308	  ordinary; only the connector's key is `$this` (`resolvable_key`, § Entities).
309	  Nothing about the type becomes referenceable from another subgraph, and no
310	  decision is needed to add one. `$this.<fk>` names the host's GraphQL
311	  field (`owner_id`, or `ownerId` when the schema camelCases it), so the
312	  host must declare the foreign key it reads.
313	- **Up to one request per parent.** The router calls the by-id operation
314	  for each parent object that selects the field; nothing is batched. That
315	  is up to one request per parent (50 songs selecting `album` is up to 50
316	  requests; the router may deduplicate identical representations). Say so
317	  in the field's doc comment, as the printed text does. When the fan-out is
318	  the problem, the `$batch` entity form below is the answer, and that one
319	  needs a decision.
320	- **The credential mirrors the by-id root field's.** A relationship field
321	  authenticates exactly the way its by-id operation's own root connector
322	  does, and `link-credential` is the lint error for any difference. When
323	  that connector authenticates only through `{{AUTH_EXPR}}` on the one
324	  `@source`, as above, the field declares no argument and no header — a
325	  `headers:` block, a `{$args.…}` or a credential-named argument on it
326	  would open a second credential path. When the root connector carries a
327	  per-call credential — an argument interpolated into a header or a query
328	  parameter, as every AppWorld service does, since it has no global
329	  credential and a type-level `@connect` sees only `$this` — the field
330	  declares the same argument (same name, same type, same nullability) and
331	  sends it the same way:
332	
333	  ```graphql
334	  owner(access_token: String!): Widget_Co_Owner
335	    @connect(
336	      source: "widget_co"
337	      http: { GET: "/owners/{$this.owner_id}", headers: [{ name: "Authorization", value: "Bearer {$args.access_token}" }] }
338	      selection: """id login"""
339	    )
340	  ```
341	
342	  when `Query.widget_co_owner(ownerId: ID!, access_token: String!)` sends
343	  `Bearer {$args.access_token}`. A missing, renamed, retyped or re-slotted
344	  argument fails authentication at runtime and is the lint error. The
345	  value may be an expression over the argument rather than a bare
346	  `{$args.<a>}` — an optional token sent with the null-preserving form
347	  `{$args.access_token->match([null, null], [@, $(['Bearer', @])->joinNotNull(' ')])}`
348	  is still the credential — and the field then declares the argument as
349	  nullable as the root does and sends the same expression verbatim. `links
350	  apply` refuses (`no-root-field`) a query credential it cannot copy
351	  exactly: one sent through a `queryParams` entry that is not exactly
352	  `$args.<a>`, or a URI pair that also reads an argument that is no
353	  credential. Write that field by hand, and note that `link-credential`
354	  compares a query credential by parameter name only. A query
355	  parameter is a credential when its name reads as one in whole words
356	  (`access_token`, `x-api-key`, `private_token`, `client_secret` — never
357	  `pageToken`, `sort_key` or `csrf_token`). `links apply --dry-run` prints
358	  whichever form applies. Either way the field adds no `@source(`: a
359	  header on a field-level `@connect` is not a source.
360	- **The selection is the by-id operation's, verbatim.** Copy the root
361	  field's `selection` unchanged so both fetch the same shape; reconcile
362	  compares both against the same operation. The root connector's static
363	  settings come along too — a static query pair on its URI
364	  (`?format=full`), every header that reads no `$args` (`Accept`) and
365	  every `queryParams` entry that reads none (`format: $("full")`) — so both
366	  reads fetch the same representation; an optional argument that is not
367	  the credential does not, nor does a constant `Authorization` header,
368	  which would open a second credential path.
369	- **A nullable foreign key carries the null guard.** Nothing
370	  in Connectors skips a field-level connector: for a parent whose fk is
371	  null the router still sends the GET, with an empty final segment
372	  (`GET /owners/`), once per distinct null parent. What answers it is
373	  whatever that path is — AppWorld answers 307 with an empty body, so
374	  every null parent failed with `CONNECTOR_FETCH` (Spotify
375	  `Spotify_QueueSong.album`: 6 of 7 queue songs; Splitwise
376	  `Splitwise_GroupsBalanceBreakdownEntry.group`: the "Non-Group Entries"
377	  row); a list endpoint answering 200 is worse, because the selection
378	  maps it into a record nobody referenced. So for an fk the host declares
379	  nullable, `links apply` prints two guards, and both are needed:
380	  `isSuccess` accepts any answer when `$this.<fk>` is null (otherwise the
381	  one `@source`'s `isSuccess`, or 2xx, decides, as before), and the
382	  selection maps to null when `$this.<fk>` is null, whatever the body
383	  holds. Under connect/v0.4 the selection goes inside the match arm
384	  (`[@, $ { … }]`, above); composition rejects the other form's nested
385	  objects there (`cannot find field`). Under connect/v0.3 it follows the
386	  match as a subselection (`…->match([null, null], [@, $]) { … }`), the
387	  only form v0.3 composes. `?! 0` reads the fk: `?!` supplies `0` only
388	  when `$this.<fk>` is absent, which the router never does (a null fk is
389	  carried as null), but `rover connector test` gives the response side no
390	  `$this` at all, and without the fallback every unit entry for the field
391	  would take the null branch. `links apply` refuses **`nullable-fk`** when
392	  the guard cannot be written: connect/v0.2 and earlier have no `?!`, and
393	  under connect/v0.3 a by-id selection holding a value that reads no
394	  response (`$("…")`, `$args`, `$this`, …) would survive a null parent as
395	  a record of nothing. A non-null fk (`owner_id: ID!`) prints no guard.
396	  Lint's `link-null-guard` warns on a relationship field whose nullable fk
397	  lacks either guard and names the missing half; re-print the field and
398	  paste its `isSuccess` and `selection`. Only make the fk non-null in the
399	  host type when the API guarantees it on every parent.
400	- **Only the GET-by-id template is a relationship field.** Reconcile and
401	  lint read a field-level `@connect` as one when it is a `GET` whose one
402	  `{$this.<fk>}` is the whole final path segment (a trailing `/` or an
403	  extension such as `.json` allowed). Any other field-level connector — a
404	  sub-resource read (`/repos/{$this.owner}/{$this.name}/issues`), a read
405	  past the id (`/x/{$this.id}/receipt`), a write — is listed under
406	  `field_connectors` and checked for nothing else.
407	- **It is a selection judgement, never a hand edit.** The `links:` entry in
408	  `selection.yaml` ([workspace-contract.md § `links`](workspace-contract.md#selectionyaml))
409	  is what makes the field expected: `graphos-factory-core selection draft`
410	  proposes one per `candidate_entity_link` fact with `confirmed: false`, you
411	  confirm it with the user, and `graphos-factory-core links apply . --dry-run`
412	  prints the field text above for you to paste into the host type. The
413	  crate never writes the schema. A field with no included entry is
414	  `links.remove` drift; a confirmed entry with no field is `links.add`.
415	
416	`links apply` refuses a confirmed entry it cannot print, and names the
417	kind. Four of them only the authored schema can tell you:
418	
419	- **`circular`** — the by-id selection, copied onto the host, selects back
420	  into a type already on its path, in practice the host (the album read
421	  copied onto `Spotify_Track.album` selects `songs { … }`, which are
422	  `Spotify_Track`s). The check walks only what that selection selects: a
423	  field it does not select never makes a link circular, even one with its
424	  own `@connect` such as the opposite link (`Widget.owner` and
425	  `Owner.favoriteWidget` both print, whichever is pasted first); a field it

427	  rejects that re-entry too. The error rover reports depends on what is
428	  pasted (rover 0.41.0, supergraph plugin 2.15.2, on copies of the AppWorld
429	  amazon and spotify workspaces): the field with the null guard `links
430	  apply` prints for a nullable fk fails `GRAPH_QL_ERROR: No matching shape

432	  … type X appears more than once in …`. The refusal message names only
433	  the second. All 5 AppWorld refusals were correct. Amazon's 4
434	  (`[]>variations[]>product_id` onto `Amazon_Product_Variation.product`)

441	  - **Trimming the copied selection** at the back-edge: a shared return

443	    composition fails `SATISFIABILITY_ERROR`.
444	  - **`@shareable`**: no change.
445	  - **The entity form** in one subgraph (`@key`, a type-level `@connect`,
446	    key stubs): `CIRCULAR_REFERENCE` and `GRAPH_QL_ERROR` both.
447	  - **`fields.exclude` of the back-edge** — what the refusal message

453	  **Only a type split composes and keeps the relationship.** Split the
454	  **target** when the host is the target's own child (amazon: `product:
455	  Amazon_VariationProduct`, whose `variations` is a new type with no link;

462	  (`Amazon_AmazonProductsByProductIdResponseVariationsItem`). A split is an
463	  authoring decision, not a `links apply` output: record it (`decide:`,
464	  `graphos-factory-core decisions add …` with declining the link as its
465	  alternative, D-id; it overrides any shared-type decision), paste the field by hand, and give it its own unit entry, e2e
466	  case, null-parent case and live case. Until those exist it is not
467	  validated. Otherwise decline the link (`include: false` with a
468	  `reason`).

470	  (its root field's selection left the property out), so `{$this.<fk>}`

472	  selection and apply it before the link.
473	- **`nullable-fk`** — the host declares the fk nullable and the null

640	### When the entity form is right
641	
642	The entity form (`@key` plus a type-level `@connect`, § Entities) is for
643	two cases: another subgraph must be able to reference the type, or the
644	fan-out of a relationship field has to be batched. Within one subgraph,
645	prefer a relationship field. Only make a type an entity when a decision
646	records why in `decisions.json` (`graphos-factory-core decisions`); entities
647	widen the supergraph's contract.
648	
649	`list_context` is false on every fact: the inventory refuses a target whose
650	response is a list. When you find such a list-returning by-id read yourself
651	(the matched parameter's own operation already returns a list), write a `$batch` type-level connector instead of a
652	singular `$this` one — the backing shape is already a list, which is what
653	`$batch` needs instead of unwrapping one item at a time. Check the target
654	first: such a read can list a collection the key *owns* rather than name
655	the key's record — before list targets were refused, gitea's `RepositoryMeta > owner` hint
656	targeted `get:/packages/{owner}`, the owner's packages — and that is no
657	relationship at all. Point the `links:` entry's `operation` and
658	`parameter` at the record's own by-id read (`get:/users/{username}`), or
659	decline it:
660	
661	```graphql
662	type Query {
663	  reviews: [Widget_Co_Review]
664	    @connect(
665	      source: "widget_co"
666	      http: { GET: "/reviews" }
667	      selection: "id rating product: { id: productId }"
668	    )
669	}
670	
671	type Widget_Co_Product
672	  @key(fields: "id")
673	  @connect(
674	    source: "widget_co"
675	    http: { GET: "/products", queryParams: "id: $batch.id" }
676	    selection: "id name"
677	    batch: { maxSize: 50 }
678	  ) {
679	  id: ID!
680	  name: String
681	}
682	```
683	
684	Each `Widget_Co_Review.product` resolves through `Widget_Co_Product`'s own
685	connector, called once per batch of `productId`s rather than once per
686	review.
687	
688	The relationship field above is the default; this is its batched variant,
689	and because it is the entity form it needs the decision.
690	
691	### Finding a `$batch` candidate
692	
693	Do not guess whether a vendor has a bulk lookup. Run
694	`graphos-factory-core batch find .` on every build. For each keyed
695	type it lists the operations that return an array of the type, and whether
696	one takes a list of the type's key. It also says how the list is passed:
697	
698	- `repeated`: `?id=1&id=2`, an array query parameter with explode on;
699	- `comma-separated`: `?ids=1,2`, an array with explode off, a path list, or
700	  a string parameter documented as comma-separated;
701	- `space-delimited` / `pipe-delimited`: `?ids=1%202` / `?ids=1|2`, a query
702	  array with `style: spaceDelimited` / `pipeDelimited`;
703	- `array`: a JSON array body property, such as Jira's `POST
704	  /rest/api/3/comment/list` with `{"ids": [...]}`.
705	
706	It reports a maximum when the key parameter itself documents one (its
707	`maxItems` or its own description; never the operation's description, and
708	never a page size), which is the connector's `batch: { maxSize: N }`. The
709	verdicts are:
710	
711	- `batchable`: write the type-level `$batch` connector against the reported
712	  operation.
713	- `partial-shape`: the only key-list lookups answer with a shape lacking
714	  some of the type's fields. A batch would fill the entity partly.
715	- `needs-scope`: the only key-list lookups need another parameter a
716	  type-level connector cannot supply, such as a path segment
717	  (`/userprofiles/{id}/…`) or a required filter.
718	- `style-conflict`: the array is declared repeated, but documented as
719	  comma-separated. Check which one the vendor accepts before writing either
720	  form.
721	- `paginated`: the only key-list lookups are paged lists. One request
722	  answers one page, so a batch larger than the page silently drops
723	  entities. Keep the `$this` connector unless the vendor documents that a
724	  key filter returns every match, and then set `maxSize` to the page size.
725	- `list-no-key-filter`: list operations exist, but none filters by the key.
726	  There is nothing to batch against, so a `$this` connector is correct.
727	- `none`: nothing returns an array of the type.
728	
729	To batch a type:
730	1. Set `graphql.batch: true` on its entity operation in `selection.yaml`.
731	2. Paste the connector `batch find` then prints over the type's header, and
732	   audit it. Map the object fields it lists by hand, and keep `@key`. No
733	   instrument writes the schema. The draft's `selection` reads the lookup's
734	   wire shape: a field the schema renames is written `amenityCategory:
735	   amenity_category`. When a scalar field has no property of that name or
736	   of its snake/kebab form, there is no draft, and the note names the
737	   field; write that selection by hand from the type's other connectors.
738	   Fields with arguments or their own `@connect` stay out of it.
739	3. Run `graphos-factory-core scaffold . --op batch:<Shape>`. The case goes
740	   through a root field whose own connector selects the key alone under the
741	   reference (`amenities { id }`). A root that maps the entity's other
742	   fields lets the planner fill them there, so the lookup is never called;
743	   with no key-only root the case is skipped with that reason. The root stub
744	   returns references carrying the key alone. The lookup stub demands the
745	   exact deduplicated key list and is `x-required`
746	   ([testing.md](testing.md)). Run `e2e.sh --generate`, then the suite. The
747	   case fails unless the router makes that one request.
748	
749	The draft is proven at e2e at `connect/v0.3` (federation 2.12.0, router
750	2.17.0). At `connect/v0.4` (federation 2.15.2, router 2.17.0) the same
751	scratch copy of the stay-listings fixture failed: the router resolved the references
752	through another Query connector on the type (`GET /listing/amenities`,
753	then `GET /amenities/listings` once that field was removed), not through
754	the `$batch` connector. The cause is a router bug, fixed on `dev` by
755	[apollographql/router#9853](https://github.com/apollographql/router/pull/9853)
756	and not yet in a release (Router 2.18.0 does not have it); see
757	[At v0.4, a `Query` connector can hijack entity resolution](#at-v04-a-query-connector-can-hijack-entity-resolution).
758	On this fixture a Mutation connector was used too: a read of
759	`userListings { id amenities { id } }` sent `POST /listings`. v0.3 is not
760	affected. Until the pinned router contains that commit, a `$batch` draft is
761	proven at v0.3 only; on v0.4 the `x-required` case catches the misroute.
762	
763	To decline, set `graphql.batch: false` and record why in `decisions.json`;
764	lint's `batchable-entity-unbatched` errors until one of the two is done.

766	`--all-types` also reports unkeyed response types, to find entities worth
767	keying. `--check` exits 1 while a batchable keyed type has no `$batch`
768	connector; a schema that does not parse exits 2. It reads the schema's
769	type-level `@connect` directives, on a type or an `extend type`, so a
770	`$batch` in a description or comment does not count. The detector matches
771	on names: a key list named for something
772	else (`?filter[id]=`, `?q=id:1,2`) is missed, so read the vendor docs when
773	the verdict looks wrong.
774	
775	## v0.3 vs v0.4
776	
777	`v0.4` is the target. Apollo documents its floor as composition 2.14.1 and
778	Apollo Router 2.15.0; the graph the subgraph joins has to meet both, not
779	just the pin the layers run at. Commas, bare numbers, unwrapped operator
780	chains and bare-brace bodies compose at 2.15.1 and 2.15.2 but not at 2.14.0
781	([mapping-language.md](mapping-language.md#what-your-pin-decides)). It brings:
782	
783	- **Abstract types**: unions and interfaces mapped from `oneOf` /
784	  `discriminator`, with a `...` spread of `->match` at a connector's own
785	  return type ([mapping-language.md](mapping-language.md#abstract-types)).
786	  On v0.3 a polymorphic payload is a documented JSON scalar
787	  ([schema-authoring.md](schema-authoring.md)).
788	- **A looser mapping grammar**: comma-separated selection lists, literals
789	  written bare after an alias (`kind: "Book"`), operator chains without `$( )`,
790	  bare-brace request bodies, and `...` spread.
791	- Not new methods. Methods arrive with router releases, not connect
792	  versions, but a breaking change to an existing method applies only from
793	  the connect version that introduced it
794	  ([mapping-language.md](mapping-language.md#which-methods-run)).
795	
796	One piece of that grammar changes meaning silently: at v0.3 a quoted string,
797	`true`, `false` or `null` after an alias reads a property of that name, and at
798	v0.4 it is a literal. [mapping-language.md](mapping-language.md) has the
799	details and how to move a v0.3 workspace with `connect-migrate`.
800	
801	## v0.5: preview, do not link
802	
803	Router 2.18.0 (2026-09-30) added `connect/v0.5` as a preview spec version.
804	The router will not start with a schema that links it unless `router.yaml`
805	sets `connectors.preview_connect_v0_5: true`. Nothing here sets that or has
806	run a v0.5 schema, so stay on v0.4 unless the user asks for v0.5, and record
807	the decision.
808	
809	Its main behaviour change: a response whose shape does not match the
810	field's type (an object where a list is declared, the reverse, or `null` for
811	a non-null field) is a `CONNECTORS_RESPONSE_SHAPE` error instead of a silent
812	`null`. At v0.4 those mismatches pass without an error, so a test has to
813	assert the mapped values, not just the absence of errors
814	([testing.md](testing.md)).
815	
816	## What connectors cannot express
817	
818	Record any of these as `unsupported` or `needs_review` in the inventory
819	rather than approximating them:
820	
821	- A non-JSON response body (NDJSON, CSV, binary, SSE streams).
822	- Query parameters whose keys are open-ended (a `deepObject` or exploded
823	  object with `additionalProperties`). A `deepObject` that declares its
824	  properties is expressible by spelling each key, quoted:
825	  `"filter[status]": $args.status`. Passing a whole input object
826	  (`filter: $args.f`) composes but fails every request at runtime.
827	- Object-valued arguments in a `rover connector test` unit entry — see
828	  [testing.md](testing.md); the write still works at runtime, it just
829	  cannot be asserted at that layer.
830	- One `@source` per workspace. Connectors allow several, but the layers
831	  render one host and one credential, so anything needing a second host or a
832	  second credential is outside the workspace model; lint reports a second
833	  `@source`, as a warning or an error depending on the target.
834
