content.content:
1037	|---|---|
1038	| `documented` | the argument's doc comment carries the sentence |
1039	| `waived` | a `behaviour` omit on a **resolved** decision or a current finding records why it does not |
1040	| `unaccounted` | neither — `--check` fails on it (`behaviour unaccounted N`) |
1041	
1042	The row's path is the source the argument reaches — `query:NAME`,
1043	`path:NAME`, `header:NAME` or `body:KEY.PATH` — and the row names the
1044	carrying argument (`Query.shop_pay(paymentCardId)`) and quotes the sentence.
1045	Fix an `unaccounted` row by writing the sentence into the doc comment, or
1046	record why not. When the sentence is not about omitting this argument (a
1047	"by default" about a server setting), the source settles it: a finding.
1048	
1049	```
1050	graphos-factory-core findings add . --title T --body TEXT --cites REF \
1051	  --omit 'get:/x|behaviour|query:sort|not-applicable'
1052	```
1053	
1054	When you chose not to state it, that is a call with stating it as the
1055	alternative: a decision.
1056	
1057	```
1058	graphos-factory-core decisions add . --title T --question Q \
1059	  --choice 'omit:leave the sentence out' --choice 'state:state it' \
1060	  --resolved --chosen omit --decision TEXT \
1061	  --omit 'get:/x|behaviour|query:sort|editorial'
1062	```
1063	
1064	`not-applicable` and `editorial` are the two reasons for a `behaviour` omit;
1065	`consumed` is a wire reason and is refused, and `findings add` refuses
1066	`editorial`. The waiver clears the sentence, not the constraint clause. It
1067	covers exactly the one source it names, and only on a resolved decision or
1068	a current finding. An argument sent through an input type
1069	(`$args.input { … }`, `$args.input.x`) has no row yet: the trace stops at the
1070	argument, so write those sentences by hand.
1071	
1072	**Do not make an optional source parameter required to get past this.** `!`
1073	on an argument whose source parameter or body key is optional is the lint
1074	error `argument-required-optional-in-source`: the caller could no
1075	longer leave it out, so the source's omission behaviour would be unreachable.
1076	Make it optional, or, when it must be required, record why with the
1077	decision form of the `behaviour` waiver above (`--omit 'get:/x|behaviour|query:x|editorial'`).
1078	
1079	**A bare `$` selection** returns the whole response, and the
1080	classifier reads it that way: `selection: "$"` on a `[String]` field over
1081	a root array of strings maps `[]`, and over an object or an array of
1082	objects maps every row beneath it as `mapped (json)`. `$ { … }` walks its
1083	sub-selection from the root, and a method on the bare `$` (`$->first`)
1084	leaves every row `unresolved`. Record no `omits` entry for a root row a
1085	bare `$` returns; one recorded before 0.5.67 still resolves, but the row
1086	now reads `mapped` first.
1087	
1088	**Every selected operation at once.** With no OP-KEY,
1089	`graphos-factory-core source-coverage . [--json] [--check]` runs the same
1090	classifier on every operation `selection.yaml` includes (`include: true`),
1091	in inventory order. Do not loop over `inventory list`: it pages, and it
1092	lists operations the selection leaves out, which need no coverage.
1093	
1094	- Text: one line per operation with both directions' counts (and
1095	  `unverified-default` / `transport-expansion-missing` when nonzero),
1096	  `FAIL` on each that misses the bar, a totals line, and `N of M selected
1097	  operations fail the bar`. It prints no rows; run the single-key form on
1098	  a failing operation to see them.
1099	- `--json`: `{"operations": [...], "totals": {...}, "failing": [...]}`.
1100	  Each entry of `operations` is byte for byte the object `source-coverage .
1101	  OP-KEY --json` prints. `totals` holds `selected`, `passing`, `failing`,
1102	  `errors` and the summed `response` and `request` counts; `failing` lists
1103	  the operation keys.
1104	- `--check`: exits 1 when any selected operation fails, with one
1105	  `source-coverage --check: OP fails — …` line per failing operation and a
1106	  count line on stderr.
1107	- An operation the classifier cannot build a report for (a selected key
1108	  missing from `inventory.json`) is listed with its error (`{"op_key",
1109	  "error"}` in `--json`), counted failing, named with its error on stderr,
1110	  and makes the run exit 1 with or without `--check`. A selection that
1111	  includes no operation, or a workspace with no `selection.yaml`, exits 1:
1112	  nothing checked is not a pass.
1113	
1114	**Stale omits.** An `omits` entry on a resolved decision or a
1115	current finding can outlive the reason for it: the schema now maps the path, a classifier
1116	upgrade now reads a `->match` it once reported `unresolved`, the envelope
1117	now reads the path (for an `editorial` entry), or a refreshed source no
1118	longer offers the path or the operation. Such an entry is **stale**:
1119	`source-coverage` counts it per direction as `stale-omit N` (JSON
1120	`stale_omit`, only when nonzero), lists it after that direction's rows as
1121	`stale omit: D-id omits `path` (direction) on OP, but …` (JSON
1122	`stale_omits`: `decision`, `operation`, `direction`, `path`, `why` —
1123	`mapped`, `consumed`, `not-offered` or `no-operation` — `message`, `fix`),
1124	and with no OP-KEY lists every stale entry in the workspace, on any
1125	operation, selected or not. It is **not part of the bar**: a stale entry
1126	leaves no offered path unaccounted, so `--check` does not fail on it.
1127	`lint` warns `stale-omit` on each, naming the decision and the row. Fix it
1128	through the log, never by hand: `graphos-factory-core decisions supersede .
1129	--id D-id`, then record any of its omits that still apply on a new
1130	resolved decision (for a finding, `graphos-factory-core findings supersede .
1131	--id F-id` and a new finding). An entry is only reported when staleness is known: a
1132	row it covers that is `unresolved` or `unverified-default` counts as
1133	needing it.
1134	
1135	**Expansion boundaries.** A response property whose inventory
1136	node carries `x-expansion` is a relationship to another node, and the walk
1137	stops there instead of unfolding the target's graph:
1138	
1139	- **unexpanded, verified default:** it offers exactly the default leaves
1140	  (`business.id`), mapped or omitted like any leaf;
1141	- **unexpanded, `unverified`:** it offers one `unverified-default` row.
1142	  Nothing in the workspace clears it; verify the default (a raw probe of the
1143	  unexpanded field, or version-specific documentation), record it with its
1144	  evidence where the source document is generated, and refresh;
1145	- **expanded on the wire** (the fields default or literal carries
1146	  `business{…}`): it offers what the expression requests, so a requested
1147	  child you do not map is `unaccounted`.
1148	
1149	To expose a child beyond the default, put the group in the fields default
1150	(§ Sparse fieldsets). Mapping the child without it is
1151	`transport-expansion-missing`. An operation with no fields parameter (any
1152	POST) cannot ask at all: expose such a child only when a resolved decision
1153	names the operation and records the path, as a backtick span
1154	(`` `owner.name` ``), as what the source is verified to send. A GET that
1155	takes and sends the fields parameter gets no such exemption; its fix is the
1156	group in the default.
1157	
1158	**The classifier reads the forms this skill recommends**:
1159	- `map->entries` over a dictionary maps the dictionary's row;
1160	- `field->match([from, to], …)` on a scalar maps `field`, as value translation
1161	  (over an object or array, without a sub-selection, it stays unresolved:
1162	  an arm can send any part of the value);
1163	- `field->map(@->match(…))` over an array of scalars maps `field`, the same
1164	  translation applied to each element; anything else inside the
1165	  map, or a method after it, stays unresolved. In a request body it is still
1166	  unresolved, as every request-side `->match` is;
1167	- a nested object literal in a request body is read key by key;
1168	- an argument sub-selection (`key: $args.x { wire: field }`) is read wire
1169	  key by wire key;
1170	- a request body that is one `$args.<name>` expression, with or without a
1171	  sub-selection (`body: "$args.input"`, `$args.input { Wire: field }`), is
1172	  classified at the request root; a body that follows that
1173	  expression with `key: expr` pairs is not, so write one form or the other;
1174	- a deeper argument path (`$args.a.b`) forwards the field it names;
1175	- a `...` spread of `disc->match(…)` arms, the abstract-type form
1176	  ([mapping-language.md § Abstract types](mapping-language.md#abstract-types)),
1177	  maps the discriminator and each arm's fields. Any other spread leaves every
1178	  path under its object that the selection does not otherwise map
1179	  `unresolved`.
1180	
1181	An `unresolved` row names the construct the classifier does not read, for
1182	example `request expression not parsed: ->map->first` or `selection method
1183	not parsed: ->entries->first`. Such a row still comes from the classifier's
1184	grammar, not from the inventory. Never hand-edit `inventory.json` to make
1185	one go away: it is facts, and `lint` reports an edit to it
1186	(`unacknowledged-inventory-edit`). Instead:
1187	- keep the idiom;
1188	- record a finding naming the operation, the unresolved paths, and the
1189	  grammar that leaves them unresolved (`findings add --cites …`: the
1190	  classifier's grammar settles it, nobody chose it);
1191	- report the operation as not verified by this layer (e2e and conformance
1192	  still prove it), never as done.
1193	
1194	Only a dropped spec construct or a depth-limit marker points at the source
1195	document. That is fixed in the pinned working copy (`codify --source`),
1196	never in `inventory.json`.
1197	
1198	An `unaccounted` leaf is not a lint nit: it is a field the source returns
1199	that no caller can ever see, and nobody decided that.
1200	
1201	Clearing one has exactly two honest endings — map the field, or record why
1202	you did not. Leaving it off on your own judgement is a decision, with
1203	exposing it as the alternative:
1204	
1205	```bash
1206	graphos-factory-core decisions add . --title "Drop the internal audit block from candidate reads" \
1207	  --question "Expose results.auditTrail on post:/candidate.info?" \
1208	  --choice 'omit:leave it off' --choice 'expose:map it as a field' \
1209	  --resolved --chosen omit --note "Internal-only; no caller has asked for it." \
1210	  --omit 'post:/candidate.info|response|results.auditTrail|editorial'
1211	```
1212	
1213	A path an expression reads is a fact, not a call — a finding:
1214	
1215	```bash
1216	graphos-factory-core findings add . --title "success is read by the @source error mapping" \
1217	  --body "The errors block reads success on every operation; it is not a field." \
1218	  --cites "references/schema-authoring.md § Errors" \
1219	  --omit 'post:/candidate.info|response|success|consumed'
1220	```
1221	
1222	`--omit operation|direction|path|reason` is repeatable on both; `direction` is
1223	`response` or `request`, `reason` is `editorial` (deliberately not exposed;
1224	a decision only — `findings add` refuses it)
1225	or `consumed` (used by an expression, not surfaced as a field). An omit on
1226	a parent path covers its children, and never matches by type name — it is a
1227	path on one operation. `.` is the root path, the whole direction: it is the
1228	only way to record an EmptyResponse 204, whose one offered row sits at the
1229	empty root (`--omit 'delete:/ecommerce/stores/{store_id}|response|.|editorial'`). The classifier reads these records back, so the same
1230	record that justifies the gap is what closes it. Never widen
1231	an omit to silence a leaf you have not actually considered; that converts a
1232	finding into a lie the next `--check` will not catch.
1233	
1234	## Writes
1235	
1236	A write operation gets the same care as a read plus two things: an explicit
1237	`graphql.root: mutation` in `selection.yaml`, and a hand-authored WireMock
1238	case, because the unit layer cannot assert an object-valued argument at all
1239	([testing.md](testing.md)). A tag an operation needs (`tags: [beta]`) is
1240	set in `selection.yaml` at selection time, not later.
1241	
1242	### Copy and update workflows
1243	
1244	A copy or clone operation reads one object and creates another. The caller
1245	must explicitly carry over any field affecting behavior or presentation —
1246	provider defaults for omitted optional fields are not "the source object's
1247	values". Identifying behavior-affecting fields: booleans and enums on the
1248	read shape that are also writable on the create or update request shape
1249	(e.g. `pinned`, `archived`, `starred`, `visibility`, `status`, `locked`,
1250	`draft`); `readOnly: true` marks fields the API never accepts on write.
1251	When the source metadata's description names the field's effect, surface it
1252	in the doc comment. Copy and clone descriptions must: (1) state they create
1253	a new object from a source; (2) list behavior-affecting fields to carry over
1254	explicitly, warning that omitted fields take provider defaults; (3) when the
1255	operation takes a full input object, warn unset keys default and do not
1256	mirror. Example: a synthetic notes API — GET /notes/{id} returns `{ id,
1257	title, content, pinned, archived, color, created_at }`, POST /notes accepts
1258	`{ title, content, pinned?, archived?, color? }`. The copy operation's
1259	description: "Creates a note. To copy an existing note, read it first and
1260	pass its title, content, pinned, archived, and color values. Fields omitted
1261	from the request take provider defaults (e.g. pinned: false), not the source
1262	note's values." The e2e case for a copy flow must demand the preserved field
1263	in the outbound body — see [testing.md](testing.md).
1264

content.content:
1	# Federation subgraph: versions, directives, composition
2	
3	A subgraph this target builds joins a supergraph the user already runs. Their
4	router and their build pipeline decide what the schema may use. The layers
5	run one pinned toolchain, and a pass at that pin says nothing yet about the
6	user's graph. Read this before `init` and before adding any Federation
7	directive beyond what the core references describe.
8	
9	## Versions: the user's graph decides, not the toolchain
10	
11	Before `init`, ask the user for two versions, and record each answer as a
12	decision (`graphos-factory-core decisions add`, then `decisions resolve` with
13	what they said):
14	
15	1. The Apollo Router version serving the supergraph. With several
16	   deployments, the oldest one counts.
17	2. The federation version the variant's build pipeline composes with (the
18	   `federation_version` of their composition, or the version GraphOS builds
19	   the variant at).
20	
21	Pick the connect spec from Apollo's documented minimums
22	([version requirements](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/graphos/connectors/getting-started/version-requirements)):
23	
24	| `connect/` | Apollo Router at least | build pipeline at least |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| `v0.4` | 2.15.0 | 2.14.1 |
27	| `v0.3` | 2.8 | 2.12 |
28	| `v0.2` | 2.3 | 2.11 |
29	| `v0.1` | 2.0 | 2.10 |
30	
31	- Use the newest connect spec that both of the user's versions meet, and
32	  never `v0.5` (a preview: connectors-language.md § v0.5). Below Router
33	  2.16.0, `v0.4` was still a preview the router had to opt into
34	  (connectors-language.md § Linking the spec); ask whether their router
35	  configuration does.
36	- Link `federation/vX.Y` no newer than the version their pipeline composes
37	  with. A link older than the workspace's `federation_version` pin is
38	  recorded as `federation_spec_version` (workspace-contract.md).
39	- `init` writes `connect/v0.4` and `federation_version: "2.15.2"`, and the
40	  layers run Apollo Router 2.17.0 (`toolchain.sh`). When the user's router
41	  is older than 2.15.0 or their pipeline older than 2.14.1, do not ask them
42	  to upgrade production to fit one subgraph. Move the workspace to `v0.3`
43	  instead: run mapping-language.md § Moving a workspace from v0.3 to v0.4
44	  in reverse. Set `connect_spec: v0.3` and a `federation_version` no newer
45	  than their pipeline (`"2.12.0"` is the pin earlier workspaces used) in
46	  `.factory/workspace.yaml` and `supergraph.yaml`, link `connect/v0.3`, and
47	  rewrite what v0.3 reads differently or cannot parse: mapping-language.md
48	  § Literals (a quoted string, `true`, `false` or `null` after an alias reads
49	  a property at v0.3), § Abstract types (no unions or interfaces; a
50	  documented JSON scalar instead) and § What v0.3 lacks. Record the move as
51	  a decision, then compose and run the e2e layer.
52	- Below Router 2.8 or a pipeline below 2.12, nothing in this skill has been
53	  run. Say so and ask the user before going further.
54	- Every report names both sides: the pins the layers ran at (connect spec,
55	  `federation_version`, router 2.17.0) and the versions the user runs. Where
56	  they differ, the layers' result is evidence at the pin only. The subgraph
57	  is unverified on the user's versions, never a pass.
58	
59	## Directives a connector subgraph may carry
60	
61	Apply each of these only after the user has answered the question it raises
62	and you have recorded the answer as a decision. Never add one speculatively,
63	"in case".
64	
65	Every directive the schema applies must be in the federation `@link`'s
66	`import` list. Compose rejects one that is not ("add "@inaccessible" to the
67	`import` argument of the @link"). Lint's `federation-drift` checks the import for the nine directives this
68	target allows (`@key`, `@shareable`, `@requires`, `@provides`, `@external`,
69	`@tag`, `@inaccessible`, `@listSize`, `@cost`); for any other directive the
70	compose layer is the check.
71	
72	Measured at `federation_version` 2.15.2 with Apollo Router 2.17.0 and no
73	license: `@inaccessible`, `@listSize` and `@cost` compose, and the router
74	starts and serves them. `@authenticated` and `@requiresScopes` compose, but
75	the router refuses to start ("license violation, the router is using
76	features not available for your license").
77	
78	- **`@inaccessible`** hides a field from clients while the router can still
79	  fetch it. Two uses:
80	  - Staging a new root field: ship it inaccessible, and remove the directive
81	    when the user says clients may use it.
82	  - Hiding a foreign-key field kept only so a relationship field can read it
83	    through `$this`. Measured: a field-level connector reading
84	    `$this.owner_id`, with `owner_id` inaccessible, resolves.
85	
86	  An e2e or live case cannot select an inaccessible field (the router
87	  answers `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED`, "Cannot query field"), so test it
88	  through the field that reads it.
89	- **`@shareable`**: only when the user's other subgraph defines the same
90	  type and field, and only after they name it. This subgraph's prefixed
91	  types never collide with another subgraph's, so the need is rare. Fields in
92	  an entity's `@key` are already shareable and need no directive.
93	- **`@listSize`** and **`@cost`**: only when the user's router enforces
94	  demand control
95	  ([demand control](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/graphos/routing/security/demand-control)),
96	  a feature tied to their plan (ask them to check theirs). On a list field
97	  whose size an argument sets, write
98	  `@listSize(slicingArguments: ["limit"])`. Add
99	  `requireOneSlicingArgument: false` when that argument is optional, because
100	  the default is `true` and the router would then reject a query that
101	  omits it. On a field returning an object that wraps the list, add
102	  `sizedFields: ["<list field>"]`. When the API fixes the page size, write
103	  `assumedSize:` instead. Take the values from the inventory, never a guess:
104	  the operation's `pagination.size_param` names the argument, and that
105	  parameter's `default` and `maximum` are the source's numbers (lint's
106	  `pagination-bounds-unknown` already warns when the source documents
107	  neither). With neither documented, ask the user for the number and record
108	  it. `@cost(weight:)` likewise: only a weight the user gives you.
109	- **`@authenticated`, `@requiresScopes`, `@policy`**: the router enforces
110	  them whichever subgraph carries them, and only with router authorization
111	  configured (JWT authentication or a coprocessor supplying the claims). The
112	  connector calls the vendor with one service credential, so every caller
113	  the supergraph lets through reads with that credential. Ask whether a field
114	  must require the router's authentication, and use only scope or policy
115	  names the router already checks. These are licensed router features: the
116	  user should check their plan, and the layers' unlicensed router does not
117	  start with them (above; `@policy` was not measured). A workspace carrying
118	  one cannot pass e2e or live today. Record the requirement as a decision,
119	  leave the directive out of the workspace schema, and tell the user it is a
120	  change they make in their own graph, outside what this skill validated.
121	- **`@tag`**: see § `@tag` and contracts.
122	- **`@key`** and the entity form are in connectors-language.md § Entities.
123	  `@requires` with `@external` on a type another subgraph owns: § Entities
124	  another subgraph owns. `@provides` is still open (§ Open).
125	
126	### Never
127	
128	- `@context` or `@fromContext`: connectors do not support them.
129	- `@cacheTag`, or any reliance on entity caching: the router's entity
130	  cache does not fully support connectors.
131	- `@connect` on a `Subscription` field: connectors serve `Query` and
132	  `Mutation` only.
133	- `@override` that moves a field from this connector subgraph back to a
134	  resolver subgraph. Connectors support `@override` only in the other
135	  direction.
136	- A `@provides` claiming fields the connector's response does not carry.
137	
138	The connector-side list is Apollo's
139	[limitations](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/graphos/connectors/reference/limitations).
140	
141	## `@tag` and contracts
142	
143	`@tag` is permitted, and off by default: it exists for
144	[GraphOS Contracts](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/graphos/platform/schema-management/delivery/contracts/overview),
145	which include or exclude types and fields by tag name. Apply it only when
146	the user's supergraph uses contracts, with the names their contracts
147	already filter on, and record that as a decision. Never invent a tag: this
148	target imposes no tag names, so `unknown-tag` never fires, and a schema
149	that applies `@tag` imports it in the federation `@link` like any other
150	directive (`federation-drift` reports one applied without the import). The
151	choice is recorded in `selection.yaml` as the operation's `tags:` list,
152	and `reconcile` checks that list against the field's `@tag(name:)`
153	directives, so the two change together.
154	
155	## Entities another subgraph owns
156	
157	The most common reason to build a subgraph for a supergraph that already
158	runs: the user's other subgraphs own an entity (`Product`, `Account`), and
159	this REST source holds data about it, keyed by the same identifier. Apollo
160	documents the pattern
161	([entities across subgraphs](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/graphos/connectors/entities/across-subgraphs)):
162	declare the owner's type with its **exact name** and its `@key`, and either
163	reference it or add fields to it. Under this target's prefix rule the
164	owner's name is a `type-prefix` error until a decision says the type is
165	another subgraph's. Lint never decides that for you, and neither do you.
166	
167	**The decision comes first.** Ask the user which subgraph owns the type,
168	its exact name, and the owner's key: its fields and their types, as the
169	owner's schema declares them (the user reads it from their graph, for
170	example with `rover subgraph fetch`). Never infer the key from the REST
171	source. Then record their answer:
172	
173	```bash
174	graphos-factory-core decisions add . --title "Account is owned by the accounts subgraph" \
175	  --question "Which subgraph owns Account, and by which key?" \
176	  --choice "the accounts subgraph, by login (String!)" --choice "this subgraph" \
177	  --foreign-type Account --resolved --chosen 1 --by user
178	```
179	
180	Only a resolved record counts. An open one lifts nothing, and lint keeps
181	the prefix and entity errors until it is resolved.
182	
183	**Two forms.** Pick the one the user's join needs, and write either by
184	hand (`links apply` does not print them; see below).
185	
186	1. **A reference stub.** This subgraph's own type points at the owner's
187	   entity, and the owner resolves every other field:
188	
189	   ```graphql
190	   type Account @key(fields: "login", resolvable: false) {
191	     login: String!
192	   }
193	
194	   type Gitea_Issue {
195	     "The account that opened the issue, resolved by the accounts subgraph."
196	     author: Account
197	     # ...
198	   }
199	   ```
200	
201	   Every connector that returns the host type builds the key in its
202	   selection (`author: user { login }`, or `author: { login: $.user.login }`).
203	   A connector that returns the host and leaves the reference out cannot
204	   serve a query that selects it.
205	2. **An extension of the owner's entity.** This subgraph adds fields to
206	   the owner's type. The `@key` is the owner's, resolvable, and each added
207	   field has its own field-level `@connect` that reads `$this.<key field>`.
208	   There is no type-level `@connect` and no root lookup:
209	
210	   ```graphql
211	   type Account @key(fields: "login") {
212	     login: String!
213	     "The Gitea user with this login, fetched through get:/users/{username}, one request per Account that selects it."
214	     giteaUser: Gitea_User
215	       @connect(
216	         source: "gitea"
217	         http: { GET: "/users/{$this.login}" }
218	         selection: """
219	         id
220	         login
221	         # ...every field of Gitea_User, as gitea_user's own selection maps it
222	         """
223	       )
224	   }
225	   ```
226	
227	   The field's selection maps every field of the type it returns: copy the
228	   by-id root field's selection verbatim. Measured: with a four-field
229	   selection the subgraph composed alone, and composed beside the owner it
230	   failed with `SATISFIABILITY_ERROR` ("cannot find field
231	   Gitea_User.loginName"). Name each added field so it cannot collide with
232	   one the owner already has (`giteaUser`, not `user`). The fields are not
233	   `@shareable`, so a shared name fails composition with the owner.
234	
235	   To read an owner's field that is not part of the key, declare it on the
236	   type with `@external` and name it in `@requires`. The connector then
237	   reads it through `$this`. Import both directives in the federation
238	   `@link`:
239	
240	   ```graphql
241	   type Product @key(fields: "id") {
242	     id: ID!
243	     weight: Int @external
244	     shippingCost(zip: String!): Int
245	       @requires(fields: "weight")
246	       @connect(source: "ship", http: { GET: "/rates?zip={$args.zip}&weight={$this.weight}" }, selection: "$.cost")
247	   }
248	   ```
249	
250	**What lint checks on a declared type.**
251	
252	- `type-prefix` does not fire on it. Root fields keep `field-prefix`.
253	- `entity-without-lookup` does not fire when every connector on the type
254	  is field-level and reads `$this`. A type-level `@connect`, or a field
255	  connector that reads only `$args`, brings the lookup rule back.
256	- `entity-without-consumer` holds only a stub: a resolvable key's consumer
257	  is the owner.
258	- `entity-field-unresolved` skips its key fields, which the
259	  representation carries, and its `@external` fields, which the owner
260	  resolves.
261	- `entity-key-not-embedded` is unchanged: an embedding that lacks the key
262	  cannot become a reference, whoever owns the type.
263	- This target adds four rules. `foreign-type-without-key` (error): a
264	  declared type with no `@key`. `foreign-type-key-field-missing` (error): a
265	  `@key` field the type does not declare. `requires-on-foreign-type`
266	  (warning): a `@requires` naming a field the type does not declare.
267	  `foreign-type-not-object` (error): the declared name is an enum, input,
268	  interface, union or scalar here. Only an object type can be an entity,
269	  so the declaration lifts nothing on it and `type-prefix` still holds it.
270	
271	An undeclared unprefixed object type keeps the `type-prefix` error, and its
272	message names the `--foreign-type` decision.
273	
274	**Testing.** An added field is a relationship field to the layers. Write
275	its unit entry by hand, with `target: "Account.giteaUser"` and
276	`variables: { $this: { login: <sample> } }` (testing.md). An extension
277	field has no e2e case in this subgraph alone: no root field here returns
278	the owner's type, and the router does not serve `_entities` to clients. So
279	`link-untested` and `link-live-unaccounted` keep warning on it. Report the
280	field as validated at the connector only, never end to end. A stub's host
281	field is tested like any other field: the e2e case selects
282	`author { login }` through the host's root field.
283	
284	**`links:` entries.** `links apply --dry-run` does not know about foreign
285	types and prints only same-subgraph relationship fields. For a link whose
286	target is the owner's entity, write the stub and the host field's
287	selection by hand, as in form 1.
288	
289	**Moving a field from a resolver subgraph into this one.** `@override`
290	moves a field in one direction only: from a subgraph with resolvers to this
291	connector subgraph, never back (§ Never). No pilot has run this recipe
292	yet, so tell the user it is Apollo's documented path and not one the layers
293	have measured. Do it in this order, with each step recorded as a decision:
294	
295	1. Declare the type foreign, and add the field to the extension with its
296	   `$this`-keyed connector and `@override(from: "<the resolver subgraph's
297	   name>")`. Import `@override` in the federation `@link`. Compose is the
298	   check: `federation-drift` does not cover `@override`.
299	2. To move traffic gradually, use
300	   `@override(from: "<name>", label: "percent(5)")` and raise the
301	   percentage step by step. Progressive override is a licensed router
302	   feature: the user should check their plan. The layers' unlicensed
303	   router cannot run it, so the label stays out of the workspace's own
304	   checks. Say so.
305	3. At 100%, remove the label. Once every router serves the new schema, the
306	   user removes the field from the resolver subgraph.
307	
308	**Still unverified** until the user's `supergraph_check` has run against
309	their graph (verification.md). The other layers compose this subgraph
310	alone, where a declared type composes with whatever key you wrote. Whether
311	that key is the owner's (same name, same fields, same types) is checked
312	only when it is composed against their graph. It is what they told you; say that it came from them.
313	Measured on the gitea pilot with a stand-in owner subgraph (`Account
314	@key(fields: "login")`, federation 2.15.2): the extension and the stub
315	each composed alone and beside the owner.
316	
317	## Open
318	
319	These are not answered yet. Do not promise them to the user and do not fake
320	them.
321	
322	- **`@provides` and `@interfaceObject`** (which connectors support from
323	  `connect/v0.4` only) on another subgraph's entities: not modelled.
324	  Entities another subgraph owns are covered above (§ Entities another
325	  subgraph owns); `links apply` does not print them yet.
326	- **Which operations become entities by default**: every GET-by-id the
327	  inventory finds, only those the user selects, or only those another
328	  selected type refers to. The `entity-*` lint rules assume this subgraph
329	  owns each entity it declares.
330	- **More than one `@source`.** Connectors allow several; the layers render
331	  one host and one credential, so this target reports a second `@source` as
332	  a warning (`multiple-sources`), its name differing from
333	  `workspace.service` a warning too (`source-name-secondary`), and turns
334	  `commented-source` off: unmodelled, not forbidden. The first source's
335	  name must still equal `workspace.service` (`source-name`, an error):
336	  `tests/router.yaml` keys the source by it, and a renamed one sends e2e
337	  to the real host. Modelling more than one would change the workspace's
338	  single `source` entry, the per-source variables and credential, and the
339	  fixtures that name a source.
340	- **The federation version.** Whether the pin should follow the user's
341	  graph instead of `init`'s default.
342

1	# Your first subgraph: the linear path
2	
3	A new workspace's first subgraph, document to `export`, in the order that
4	works: per step the commands, what to check, and the reference to read when
5	it does not match. `SKILL.md` stays the authority. Commands run from the
6	workspace root as `graphos-factory` (the shared references write
7	`graphos-factory-core`); `$S` is the scripts directory `env.sh` exports;
8	examples are Swagger Petstore v3. An exit marked **expected** is no stop.
9	
10	## 0. Before the first command
11	
12	- `bash <skill>/scripts/bootstrap.sh --check` (on 127, run it without
13	  `--check`), then `. <skill>/scripts/env.sh`.
14	- Ask the user, and wait for each answer:
15	  1. **The Elastic License v2** (https://www.elastic.co/licensing/elastic-license):
16	     only on an explicit yes, prefix the wrappers and `evidence` with
17	     `APOLLO_ELV2_LICENSE=accept`. Without it compose, unit, e2e and live
18	     are `not_run`, and nothing validates.
19	  2. **The toolchain**: when `bash $S/toolchain.sh --check` exits 1, ask
20	     before `bash $S/toolchain.sh` (the plugin and the Router only once the
21	     licence is accepted; Java 17+ is theirs).
22	  3. **Versions**: their Router (the oldest deployment) and their build
23	     pipeline's federation version. `init` pins `connect/v0.4`, which needs
24	     Router 2.15.0 and pipeline 2.14.1 (federation-subgraph.md § Versions).
25	- `context_mode`: `generic` for a generic wrapper (SKILL.md step 3). Fetch
26	  the document yourself; the binary never fetches.
27	
28	Record nothing before step 1: `decisions add` in an empty directory creates
29	`.factory/`, and `init` then refuses the directory as a workspace.
30	
31	## 1. `init`
32	
33	```bash
34	graphos-factory init <dir> --name <name> --spec openapi.json --url <where you fetched it> --context-mode generic
35	cd <dir> && git init && git add -A && git commit -m "init: <name>"   # inside a repo: no git init
36	```
37	
38	It lists `.factory/` (workspace, sources, inventory with its counts), the
39	working copy, and four skeletons: `<directory>.graphql` (links and the one
40	`@source`, no root field), `template.yaml`, `supergraph.yaml`,
41	`tests/router.yaml`. Act on every comment in `template.yaml` and the header:
42	
43	- **Relative server** (`/api/v3`): `BASE_URL` is the stand-in
44	  `http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v3`. Keep it; the production host comes at `export`.
45	- **Several security schemes**: the `AUTH_EXPR` comment names the one it
46	  describes; ask which the subgraph sends, and record it. A key sent bare in
47	  its own header (`value: "{{AUTH_EXPR}}"`) draws `quoted-auth-expr`.
48	- **No security scheme**: delete the Authorization header from `@source`
49	  and the `AUTH_EXPR` entry from `template.yaml`.
50	
51	Now record the step 0 answers as decisions (step 3) and the licence consent
52	in `.factory/memory.md`. Read: workspace-contract.md § Creating a workspace.
53	
54	## 2. What the API offers
55	
56	`graphos-factory inventory list` (50 a page: follow `--offset
57	<next_offset>` until it is null) and `inventory describe <op-key>`. `?` is
58	needs_review (the reason beneath), `x` unsupported, `[read?]` a POST whose
59	name suggests a read: ask about each, since a POST is a write until the
60	user says otherwise. `links:` lines feed step 4. Read: spec-intake.md.
61	
62	## 3. Agree the selection, and write it down
63	
64	Agree each operation in or out, its root and its name. Each judgement is a
65	decision; `add` prints `N  label` per choice, and `--chosen` takes the N:
66	
67	```bash
68	graphos-factory decisions add . --title "First release scope" --question "Which operations?" --choice "reads only" --choice "reads and writes"
69	graphos-factory decisions resolve . --id D-xxxxxx --chosen 1 --note "what the user said" --by user
70	```
71	
72	No command creates `.factory/selection.yaml`; write it:
73	
74	```yaml
75	contract_version: 2
76	defaults: { fields: all, max_depth: 6, opaque_json_policy: forbid }
77	operations:
78	  get:/pet/{petId}:
79	    include: true
80	    graphql: { root: query, name: pet }   # camelCase, unprefixed: the field is petstore_pet
81	  "post:/pet": { include: false, reason: "read-only first release" }
82	```
83	
84	A name with an underscore is refused (`^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`). Read:
85	workspace-contract.md § `selection.yaml`.
86	
87	## 4. `selection draft`, then confirm
88	
89	`graphos-factory selection draft .` adds a `response.envelope` per included
90	operation and a `links:` entry per candidate fact, all `confirmed: false`.
91	Confirm each with the user (`confirmed: true`; a link may instead be
92	`include: false` with a `reason`). Without `selection.yaml`, `draft` exits
93	1 and `reconcile` exits 2 advising `selection draft`: write the file first.
94	Read: connectors-language.md § Relationship fields.
95	
96	## 5. The first apply
97	
98	| **Expected** on a fresh workspace | Exit | Why |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| `graphos-factory lock . --check` | 3 | "no .factory/applied.lock.yaml": nothing to codify yet |
101	| `graphos-factory context check .` | 0 | generic (a specialized workspace resolves its gaps first) |
102	| `graphos-factory reconcile . --baseline HEAD` | 1 | "N operations to apply", every span `added` |
103	| `bash $S/compose.sh .` | 1 | `QUERY_ROOT_MISSING`: no root field yet |
104	| `graphos-factory lint .` | 1 | `missing-field` per included operation until its root field exists; `no-applied-lock` and `no-evidence` warn until step 9 |
105	
106	Write the schema under the header: a `<TypePrefix>_<Name>` type per shape,
107	a root field with its `@connect` per operation. An `int64` id argument is
108	`ID`; an `int64` output is `String` mapped with `->match([null, null], [@,
109	@->jsonStringify])` (schema-authoring.md § Scalar choice). Done when
110	`reconcile` ends `reconcile: clean` (exit 0) and `compose: pass`. Read:
111	connectors-language.md § `@connect`, mapping-language.md.
112	
113	## 6. Relationship fields
114	
115	`graphos-factory links apply . --dry-run` prints each confirmed link's
116	field: paste it into the host type it names, re-run `reconcile`. A refused
117	entry (`circular`, `self`, `no-fk-field`, `field-exists`, `nullable-fk`,
118	`no-host`, `no-root-field`, `target-refused`) exits 1. Write its tests:
119	
120	- a unit entry, `target: "<Type>.<field>"`, `variables: { $this: { <fk>:
121	  "7" } }`, asserting the request and a `connectorResponse` (the
122	  `apiResponseBody` carries every property the selection names);
123	- an e2e case selecting the parent and the field: add it to the `x-cases`
124	  of the parent's and the by-id stubs, keeping their own;
125	- for a field printed with the null guard: a null-parent case whose parent
126	  stub omits the fk (a `null` fails conformance unless the spec allows it),
127	  a stub for the empty-segment GET (`/pet/`), and `graphos-factory codify .
128	  --waive <that stub> --status unmatched --reason R`.
129	
130	Read: connectors-language.md § Relationship fields.
131	
132	## 7. Tests: scaffold, audit, generate
133	
134	```bash
135	graphos-factory scaffold .
136	bash $S/e2e.sh . --generate && bash $S/e2e.sh . && bash $S/unit.sh .
137	graphos-factory scaffold . --op <key> --status all-missing   # per operation, then --generate again
138	```
139	
140	Audit every placeholder before `--generate`: valid is not meaningful. An
141	integer-backed `ID` gets an integer literal (`petId: 1`) the API must
142	accept. A `unit-no-response` note: write that `connectorResponse` by hand.
143	Read every snapshot for `redacted`, `valueCompletion` and `errors`. Exit 3
144	from the error scaffold refused a status whose stub would match an existing
145	one: hand-write that case with a distinct matcher (another argument value;
146	a WireMock scenario for a call with none) and `# expect-upstream-status:
147	CODE` first. `graphos-factory error-statuses .` shows what is owed. Read:
148	testing.md § Scaffolding the tests, § Error cases.
149	
150	## 8. The offline checks
151	
152	```bash
153	graphos-factory validate .                 # no fail, no unmatched; unchecked is reported, never a pass
154	graphos-factory source-coverage . --check  # "0 of N selected operations fail the bar"
155	graphos-factory lint .                     # 0 errors (schema-authoring.md § Coverage, testing.md)
156	```
157	
158	## 9. `lock`, then `evidence`
159	
160	```bash
161	graphos-factory lock .            # --model only with the identifier the host supplies
162	git add -A && git commit -m "apply: <what changed>"
163	graphos-factory evidence . --scripts $S
164	git add .factory/evidence && git commit -m "apply: evidence"
165	```
166	
167	`lock --check --provenance` exiting 3 on provenance drift alone (a case, a
168	stub, `selection.yaml`) means relock; a changed span means codify first
169	(SKILL.md, "Hand edits"). `evidence` records a hash of every file its
170	layers read, and `export` refuses any of them changed since: run `evidence`
171	last, after your final edit (a commit is not required). Only `pass` is a
172	pass. The `operations:` line counts selected operations with executed
173	evidence; a `not validated:` line names each without, and its absence is
174	the only all-clear. `live` is `not_run` without `tests/live.yaml` and the
175	credential (testing.md § Live smoke tests); `supergraph_check` is `not_run`
176	until the user's `APOLLO_KEY` and a graph ref are both there: ask once
177	which `<graph>@<variant>` and set `GRAPHOS_FACTORY_GRAPH_REF` on the run
178	(verification.md). Report each `not_run` as not run.
179	
180	## 10. `export`
181	
182	Ask the user for the production base URL, base path included (Petstore:
183	`/api/v3`), then run `graphos-factory export . --out <dir outside the
184	workspace> --base-url <that URL>`. Hand the user its output: the `rover
185	subgraph check` and `publish` commands they run with their own credentials,
186	the router minimum and credential variables, and the "Not verified by this
187	export" list, which you report as not verified. Never run rover yourself.
188	Read: export-graphos.md.
189	
190	## When something refuses
191	
192	| Refusal | Fix |
193	|---|---|
194	| `evidence-stale` (export) | re-run `evidence`: it names each file changed, added or removed since the last run |
195	| `base-url-local` (export) | the test default is this machine: `--base-url` with the production host the user gave |
196	| `--out … is inside the workspace` (export) | a directory outside the workspace |
197	| `unacknowledged-edit` (lint, `lock --check`) | yours, in this apply: `lock`; anyone else's: codify it (SKILL.md, "Hand edits") |
198	| `missing-template` (lint) | restore `template.yaml` (`git checkout --` it; its shape: workspace-contract.md § The local-validation files) |
199	| `fixture-overlap` (lint) | add the `absent` matchers it names to the broader stub, or give the narrower one a priority |
200	| `unproven-operation` (lint) | a selected operation with no evidence row: re-run `evidence` |
201	| `pagination-bounds-unknown` (lint) | write "no documented maximum" in the size argument's doc comment |
202	| `quoted-auth-expr` (lint) | right only for a key the API takes with no scheme; otherwise `Bearer {{AUTH_EXPR}}` |
203	| ELv2 `not_run` (compose, unit, e2e, live) | ask once (step 0); on a yes, prefix with `APOLLO_ELV2_LICENSE=accept` |
204

380	does not, and `selection draft` and `selection set` splice into a file that
381	already exists. `selection draft` proposes a `response.envelope` only for
382	operations the file already marks `include: true`, and on a fresh workspace
383	it exits 1 with a message that names the missing `.factory/selection.yaml` and
384	states the `include: true` requirement. The operations, their roots and names are
385	the select verb's judgements. Field paths use the same
386	`>`-separated path grammar the existing UI emits
387	(`get:/animals/{animalId}>**` means "everything under this operation").
388	
389	```yaml
390	contract_version: 2             # 2 adds `context` on overrides and waivers; a version-1 file is still read
391	defaults:
392	  fields: all                 # all | none — what an included operation selects by default
393	  max_depth: 6
394	  opaque_json_policy: forbid  # forbid | allow_with_reason — an undocumented JSON field fails lint under forbid
395	  null_handling: omit         # omit | send_null — what an explicit null argument sends; optional, a decisions.json entry overrides it per argument
396	operations:
397	  get:/v2/incidents:
398	    include: true
399	    response:
400	      envelope: incidents     # the root key the payload sits under, or null for none
401	      confirmed: true         # false while it is still `selection draft`'s proposal
402	    graphql:
403	      root: query             # query | mutation; explicit, never derived from HTTP method
404	      name: listIncidents     # semantic name; default is the sanitized operation_id
405	      description: null       # override; default from summary, else description (discovery specs have no summaries)
406	    fields:
407	      exclude:
408	        - "incidents[]>external_issue_reference"     # per-field exclusion; every array segment is spelled with [] (`_links[]`, `incidents[]>x`, `[]>x` under a root-array response): a path missing one excludes nothing, and reconcile reports it with the spelling that matches, as far as the inventory's top-level and envelope-item paths reach
409	      rename:
410	        "incidents[]>incident_status": status
411	      tags:
412	        "incidents[]>creator>email": [internal-low]
413	    pagination: { expose: [page_size, after], next_cursor: "pagination_meta.after" }
414	  post:/v2/incidents:
415	    include: true
416	    graphql: { root: mutation, name: createIncident }
417	    tags: [beta]
418	  get:/v2/incidents/{id}:
419	    include: true
420	    graphql: { root: query, name: incident, entity: true, key: id }
421	  post:/v2/incidents/{id}/actions:
422	    include: false
423	    reason: "customer asked for read-only in first release"   # shows up in COVERAGE / README
424	  # A bulk exclusion reads better as a one-line flow entry, and is equally
425	  # valid. `graphos-factory-core selection set` edits either form in place — it
426	  # replaces just the `include` value's bytes and leaves the reason, the
427	  # quoting, the spacing and the key order exactly as written.
428	  # Keep a flow entry on ONE line: a `{ … }` wrapped across lines is legal
429	  # YAML but `selection set` refuses it and tells you to unwrap it.
430	  "delete:/v2/incidents/{id}": { include: false, reason: "read-only in first release" }

432	  # Hand edits, codified (written by `graphos-factory-core codify`). Each names a
433	  # schema span, says why (`reason`, and `context` from --context), and
434	  # asserts what must stay true; `decision:` (optional, D-0019 or D-k7m2qx) names a
435	  # real decision only when the edit carries one out. Drift
436	  # between selection and schema on these is reported,
437	  # not fixed; the agent may still change the span when the selection or
438	  # inventory changes, as long as every assertion holds.
439	  - key: get:/v2/incidents/{id}
440	    reason: "severity is read first; the engineer ordered the selection by hand"
441	    context: "the on-call dashboard renders the first field as the row title"
442	    assert:
443	      - contains: "severity   # first"
444	      - tag: internal
445	    until: "incident.io returns fields in a stable order"    # free text, for humans
446	    expires: "2027-01-01"                                     # machine-checked: reported as expired after this
447	```
448	
449	**`response`** is where the envelope judgement lives: `envelope`
450	names the single root property the payload's useful content sits under, or is
451	`null` when the field returns the whole body. It must name a root property of
452	the operation's response shape — `reconcile` and lint both refuse one that
453	names nothing (`unknown-envelope`), because a typo would otherwise flatten
454	the field to a type with no fields. `graphos-factory-core selection draft`
455	proposes one per included operation from the inventory's response facts and
456	marks it `confirmed: false` — as it proposes each `links:` entry below;
457	while it is false, `reconcile` names it as still the tool's draft and lint warns (`response-envelope-unconfirmed`). An
458	operation with no `response` block at all falls back to the suggestion, and
459	`reconcile` says which one it used (`no-response-envelope`). An absent
460	`confirmed` means confirmed: a hand-written selection is the user's word.
461	
462	**`response.referenced_shape`** is a different judgement in the same block:
463	which branch of a two-branch success/error `oneOf`/`anyOf`
464	response is the actual payload, for a case the source document itself
465	leaves ambiguous. `inventory build` already writes the same key as a
466	*fact* when the source makes the branches distinguishable on its own (one
467	branch's shape also documented at an explicit non-2xx status, or both
468	branches pinning a shared boolean property to the opposite literal) — never
469	from a property's name alone. When `inventory.json` has no such fact for a
470	known two-branch response and a human or agent has reviewed the case,
471	recording the same key here (a `#/shapes/<Name>` pointer, the grammar
472	`shape_ref` already uses) resolves the finding without ever touching
473	`inventory.json`: `reconcile`'s `root_properties` and `scaffold`'s response
474	body both read the inventory fact first and fall back to this judgement
475	only when the fact is absent. Absent both, the response types as the
476	workspace's JSON scalar and the finding stays open — `scaffold` says so in
477	a note.
478	
479	**Field paths** are rooted at the response body and use a
480	`>`-separated grammar with `[]` after a list segment:
481	`incidents[]>incident_number` for an item field in a paginated list,
482	`incident>pending_actions` for a field under a single-object envelope,
483	`more` for a top-level field. An operation that returns the type shares
484	the exclusions of every other operation that returns it — write them on
485	each (YAML anchors keep them in one place); `graphos-factory-core reconcile` reports the
486	selection that says "all fields" while the connector maps fewer.
487	
488	**`overrides`** carry the engineer's intent. A key names a *span* of the
489	schema — an inventory operation key (its root field or fields), `type:<Name>`
490	(a type, enum, input, union or scalar with its doc and comments), `Query.<f>`
491	/ `Mutation.<f>` (a root field the inventory does not explain) or `header`
492	(everything before the first type). `graphos-factory-core reconcile` lists each
493	override's drift from the selection in its own section, never counts it as
494	work, and checks its assertions against the span's current text:
495	`contains` / `not_contains` (runs of whitespace compare equal), `matches`
496	(a regex), `tag`, `arg` / `no_arg` (root fields), `field` / `no_field`
497	(types). A failing assertion is not clean. An override with no assertions
498	is **pinned**: the span is compared byte-for-byte against `--baseline` and
499	the agent must not change it — lint warns, because a pin freezes the
500	operation forever; assertions are what let it keep evolving. `until` is
501	free text saying when to revisit; `expires` (YYYY-MM-DD) is checked, and an
502	expired override is reported and is not clean. `customized` (the old
503	list of fenced operations) is retired; reconcile and lint refuse it.
504	
505	**`links`** are the relationship fields the user chose to expose — a
506	property that carries another resource's id becomes a field on its host
507	type, resolved by that resource's GET-by-id operation through a
508	field-level `@connect` keyed by `$this` (no `@key`). One entry per
509	relationship, keyed by the inventory shape and the property's path:
510	
511	```yaml
512	links:
513	  - shape: Song                          # #/shapes/Song, the shape that carries the foreign key
514	    path: album_id                       # the property's path from the shape's root, wire names
515	    operation: "get:/albums/{album_id}"  # the by-id operation the field resolves through; must be included
516	    parameter: album_id                  # its trailing path parameter (wire name); defaults to the fact's
517	    field: album                         # the GraphQL field on the host type; camelCase
518	    include: true
519	    confirmed: false   # drafted by `graphos-factory-core selection draft`
520	```
521	
522	`shape`, `path`, `operation` and `parameter` restate the inventory's
523	`candidate_entity_link` fact (what the property matched); `field`,
524	`include`, `confirmed`, `reason` and `decision` (`D-0019` or `D-k7m2qx`) are the
525	judgement. `path` is the inventory walker's grammar: wire-name segments
526	joined by `>`, each followed by one `[]` per list level — `album_id` for a
527	top-level property, `[]>album_id` under a root-array shape,
528	`songs[]>album_id` for a property of a nested list's items,
529	`matrix[][]>owner_id`, `owner>account_id`. The host GraphQL type is not
530	recorded: `graphos-factory-core reconcile` derives it from the included
531	operations that return the shape, their root fields' return types and the
532	path, and reports when it cannot.
533	
534	`graphos-factory-core selection draft` appends one entry per surviving fact with
535	`confirmed: false` (`--links` drafts only links, `--envelopes` only
536	envelopes, neither both; the two together are a usage error, exit 1). It
537	never touches a fact whose `<shape> > <path>` already has an entry, in any
538	state: it skips it and says why (`already has a links entry (--force
539	replaces it)`, `already has a confirmed links entry (--force replaces only
540	a draft)`, `already has a declined links entry (include: false)`).
541	`--force` redraws an entry only while it is still `confirmed: false`. Two
542	facts on one object that would derive the same field name get distinct
543	ones — the second `<derived><FkCamel>` (`ownerSellerId`). A `links:`
544	section it cannot index line by line (the entry count it walks differs
545	from the count the file parses to) is left byte-identical and every fact
546	is skipped with that reason. `selection review` lists `unconfirmed_links`.
547	An unconfirmed entry never governs — it is a reconcile note and a
548	`link-unconfirmed` lint warning, not drift. Once confirmed,
549	`graphos-factory-core links apply . --dry-run` prints the field text to paste

552	entry declares as `links.remove`, and a wrong operation, verb or `$this`
553	variable as `links.change`. A confirmed entry the current rules no

562	Resolved `keep` is the exemption; resolved `drop` means setting

#
# This file is the artifact: edit it directly. Selection lives in
# .factory/selection.yaml, the reasoning in the decision log
# (.factory/decisions/).
#
# Auth: Authorization: Bearer <credential>; the scheme prefix stays outside AUTH_EXPR.

extend schema
  @link(url: "https://specs.apollo.dev/federation/v2.15", import: ["@key"])
  @link(url: "https://specs.apollo.dev/connect/v0.4", import: ["@source", "@connect"])

@source(
  name: "lumen_books"
  http: {
    baseURL: "{{BASE_URL}}"
    headers: [
      { name: "Authorization", value: "Bearer {{AUTH_EXPR}}" }
      { name: "Accept", value: "application/json" }
      { name: "Content-Type", value: "application/json" }
      { name: "User-Agent", value: "graphos-factory" }
    ]
  }
  errors: {
    message: "$.message ?? 'Lumen Books request failed'"
    extensions: """
    code: $.code
    httpStatus: $status
    """
  }
)

"Currency of a book's price."
enum Lumen_Books_Currency {
  USD
  EUR
  GBP
}

"Lifecycle status of an order."
enum Lumen_Books_OrderStatus {
  pending
  paid

  cancelled
}

"Customer loyalty tier."
enum Lumen_Books_CustomerTier {
  standard

  title: String
  authorId: ID
  isbn: String
  priceCents: Int
  currency: Lumen_Books_Currency
  genres: [String]
  publishedAt: String
  stock: Int
}

"A book author. An entity keyed by id (D-qbc6qk)."
type Lumen_Books_Author @key(fields: "id") {
  id: ID!
  name: String
  bio: String

}

type Lumen_Books_BookPage {

  "The page number this page holds, from 1."
  page: Int
  "The page size the API applied."
  limit: Int
  "Total number of books across all pages."

}

(D-4yyj7v).
"""

  id: ID!
  name: String
  tier: Lumen_Books_CustomerTier

}

"One line of an order."
type Lumen_Books_OrderItem {
  bookId: ID
  quantity: Int
  unitPriceCents: Int
}

"A card payment."
type Lumen_Books_CardPayment {
  type: Lumen_Books_PaymentType
  last4: String
  brand: String
}

"A bank-account payment."
type Lumen_Books_BankPayment {
  type: Lumen_Books_PaymentType
  iban: String
}

"How an order is paid: a card or a bank account, told apart by `type`."
union Lumen_Books_Payment = Lumen_Books_CardPayment | Lumen_Books_BankPayment

"An order."
type Lumen_Books_Order {
  id: ID!
  customerId: ID
  status: Lumen_Books_OrderStatus
  items: [Lumen_Books_OrderItem]
  totalCents: Int
  createdAt: String

  one request per Lumen_Books_Order that selects it: a union cannot be mapped
  inside another type's selection at connect/v0.4.

      source: "lumen_books"
      http: { GET: "/orders/{$this.id}" }
      selection: """
      $.payment {
        ... type->match(
          ["card", { __typename: "Lumen_Books_CardPayment", type, last4, brand }],
          ["bank", { __typename: "Lumen_Books_BankPayment", type, iban }],

}

type Query {
  """
  List books. Page-number pagination. `ids` fetches several books in one call.
  Retrieves one page of books. Iterate through all pages to get the complete
  collection: use the total field to know when all records have been fetched,
  or iterate until a short or empty page.
  Returns: data, page, limit, total.
  Each item in `data` has: id, title, authorId, isbn, priceCents, currency,
  genres, publishedAt, stock, author.
  """
  lumen_books_books(
    """
    1-based page number (records skipped = (page - 1) * limit; provider default: 1, min 1). When the page size changes mid-iteration, restart at page 1: continuing at the old page skips records.
    """
    page: Int
    "Page size (provider default: 10, maximum: 50). Values above 50 are rejected."
    limit: Int
    "Only books in this genre."
    genre: String
    "Comma-separated book ids. If not passed, all books are listed."
    ids: String
  ): Lumen_Books_BookPage
    @connect(
      source: "lumen_books"
      http: {
        GET: "/books"
        queryParams: """
        page: $args.page
        limit: $args.limit
        genre: $args.genre
        ids: $args.ids
        """
      }
      selection: """
      data {
        id
        title
        authorId
        isbn
        priceCents
        currency
        genres
        publishedAt
        stock
      }
      page: meta.page
      limit: meta.limit
      total: meta.total
      """
    )

  """
  Get one book.
  Returns: id, title, authorId, isbn, priceCents, currency, genres,
  publishedAt, stock, author { id, name, bio, born }.
  """
  lumen_books_book(bookId: ID!): Lumen_Books_Book
    @connect(
      source: "lumen_books"
      http: { GET: "/books/{$args.bookId}" }
      selection: """
      id
      title
      authorId
      isbn
      priceCents
      currency
      genres
      publishedAt
      stock
      """
    )

  Search books. A POST that only reads, so it sits under Query (D-jnm0uf).
  Retrieves one page of books. Use the total field to know when all records
  have been fetched, or iterate until a short or empty page.
  Returns: data, page, limit, total.
  Each item in `data` has: id, title, authorId, isbn, priceCents, currency,
  genres, publishedAt, stock, author.
  """
  lumen_books_searchBooks(
    query: String
    genre: String
    maxPriceCents: Int
  ): Lumen_Books_BookPage
    @connect(
      source: "lumen_books"
      http: {
        POST: "/books/search"
        body: """
        {
          query: $args.query?,
          genre: $args.genre?,
          maxPriceCents: $args.maxPriceCents?
        }
        """
      }
      selection: """
      data {
        id
        title
        authorId
        isbn
        priceCents
        currency
        genres
        publishedAt
        stock
      }
      page: meta.page
      limit: meta.limit
      total: meta.total
      """
    )

  """
  Get one author.
  Returns: id, name, bio, born.
  """
  lumen_books_author(authorId: ID!): Lumen_Books_Author
    @connect(
      source: "lumen_books"
      http: { GET: "/authors/{$args.authorId}" }
      selection: """
      id
      name
      bio
      born
      """
    )

  Get one customer. Email and phone are not exposed (D-4yyj7v).
  Returns: id, name, tier, createdAt.
  """
  lumen_books_customer(customerId: ID!): Lumen_Books_Customer

      source: "lumen_books"
      http: { GET: "/customers/{$args.customerId}" }
      selection: """

      name
      tier
      createdAt

  unitPriceCents, book }, totalCents, createdAt, payment.
  """

    "Only this customer's orders."
    customerId: ID
    "Only orders in this status (one of pending|paid|shipped|cancelled)."
    status: Lumen_Books_OrderStatus
    "Cursor from the previous page."
    after: String
    "Page size (provider default: 10, maximum: 50). Values above 50 are rejected."
    limit: Int

    @connect(
      source: "lumen_books"
      http: {
        GET: "/orders"
        queryParams: """
        customerId: $args.customerId
        status: $args.status
        after: $args.after
        limit: $args.limit
        """

      selection: """
      data {
        id
        customerId
        status

          quantity
          unitPriceCents

        createdAt

      """
    )

  """
  Get one order.
  Returns: id, customerId, status, items { bookId, quantity, unitPriceCents,
  book }, totalCents, createdAt, payment.
  """
  lumen_books_order(orderId: ID!): Lumen_Books_Order
    @connect(
      source: "lumen_books"
      http: { GET: "/orders/{$args.orderId}" }
      selection: """
      id
      customerId
      status
      items {
        bookId
        quantity
        unitPriceCents

      createdAt

  Returns: id, name, webhookUrl.

  lumen_books_integration(integrationId: ID!): Lumen_Books_Integration
    @connect(

          items: $args.items {

            quantity

            type
            last4

      status

        quantity
        unitPriceCents
      }
      totalCents
      createdAt
      """
    )

  """
  Change an order's status.
  Returns: id, customerId, status, items { bookId, quantity, unitPriceCents,
  book }, totalCents, createdAt, payment.
  """
  lumen_books_updateOrder(
    orderId: ID!
    "One of pending|paid|shipped|cancelled."
    status: Lumen_Books_OrderStatus!
    note: String
  ): Lumen_Books_Order
    @connect(
      source: "lumen_books"
      http: {
        PATCH: "/orders/{$args.orderId}"

      selection: """
      id
      customerId
      status
      items {
        bookId
        quantity
        unitPriceCents
      }
      totalCents
      createdAt
      """
    )

  """

  true when the cancellation succeeded and an error otherwise.
  """
  lumen_books_cancelOrder(orderId: ID!): Boolean

      source: "lumen_books"
      http: { DELETE: "/orders/{$args.orderId}" }
      selection: "$(true)"

description: Reading .claude/skills/graphos-factory/graphos-factory-core/references/testing.md

content.content:
690	  one-element array. An explicit `null` still goes through the map
691	  (`{id: null, type: "x"}`, measured on pagerduty): to drop that too, guard the
692	  argument, `$args.priorityId?->map({ id: @, type: "x" })->first`.
693	
694	- **Every `$args` scalar reaches the connector as a string.**
695	  `escalationLevel: 2` under `variables.$args` becomes `"escalation_level":
696	  "2"` in the asserted body — not what the router sends for an `Int`. Keep
697	  Int and Boolean arguments that land in a JSON body out of unit entries and
698	  prove them at e2e (pagerduty `update_incident_escalate`). Query parameters
699	  are unaffected: they are strings on the wire anyway.
700	- **`#` comments inside a `selection` string are fine** for compose, the
701	  unit framework and the router; an engineer's annotated reorder is a real
702	  edit `graphos-factory-core reconcile --baseline` must preserve, not a formatting quirk.
703	
704	## What lint and the write-body-proof layer demand of the tests themselves
705	
706	These lint rules read the unit suites and the entity keys, and warn (or
707	fail, where marked) when a test or a key exists but proves less than it
708	looks like it does:
709	
710	| Rule | What it wants | Why |
711	|---|---|---|
712	| `unit-no-credential` | every unit entry that asserts the request also asserts the credential header (the `@source` header carrying `{{AUTH_EXPR}}`) | the one header every request must carry |
713	| `unit-no-response` | every operation with unit entries has at least one asserting `connectorResponse` | request shape proven, mapping back not |
714	| `failure-case-missing` (warning; one finding per operation listing its open statuses, per-status detail in `--json`) | every non-2xx status the inventory documents for a selected operation has an e2e case calling its root field behind the case's own stub answering that status to the operation's own request (its method and path template; a nested lookup answering it does not count) (`4XX` any 4xx, `default` any non-2xx); unit entries do not count, since no suite sets a response status | an `errors` mapping that maps a 404 nobody returns is untested, however right it reads |
715	| `entity-without-lookup` (error) | each resolvable `@key` of a type is served by a selected operation that returns the type and takes that key (a path/query parameter named for it, a by-id last path segment ending with it, or a body property on a read), or by a bulk lookup batch find rates `batchable` on that key; a `resolvable: false` key needs none | nothing can resolve a reference by that key |
716	| `entity-key-not-embedded` (error) | wherever a connector's selection embeds a `@key` type, what it builds carries every field of at least one key, read through the selection (`pet { id: pet_id }`, `owner: user { … }`, `pet: { id: petId }`) at the wire path it reaches; a spread, method chain or `$this` is not judged | the router cannot turn that embedding into a reference |
717	| `entity-without-consumer` (warning) | some root field or field of another type returns the `@key` type | the key serves no reference in this subgraph |
718	| `entity-field-unresolved` (warning) | every field of a `@key` type is mapped by a connector selection that reaches the type, or has its own `@connect`; not checked on a `resolvable: false` stub | a resolved reference comes back without it |
719	
720	**`graphos-factory-core serialization`**, wired as the `write_body_proof`
721	evidence layer next to `connector_unit` and `wiremock_e2e`,
722	replaced four earlier lint rules — `list-arg-unproven`, `mutation-cases`,
723	`loose-write-body`, `unit-no-body` — that only sampled the test *shape*
724	(does a case file pass every argument, is the stub's matcher exact) rather
725	than proving *placement*: a dropped argument whose value happened to recur
726	elsewhere in the same demanded body passed all four (`crate/tests/integration/lint.rs`,
727	`the_new_layer_catches_a_dropped_argument_whose_value_recurs_elsewhere_the_old_lints_miss`).
728	The layer reads where the connector puts every argument (a body pointer, a
729	query key, a path or header placeholder) and requires an executed e2e case
730	whose stub demands the case's value *there*, not merely somewhere in the
731	body or URL. It also requires a case proving each optional body argument's
732	key absent when omitted, and, for explicit `null`, a stated behavior plus a
733	case proving it: the workspace's `defaults.null_handling` in
734	`selection.yaml` (state `omit`, "do not touch", unless the vendor needs
735	`send_null`, "clear"), overridden per argument by
736	`decisions add --null-handling 'op|arg|behavior'` (behavior: send_null or
737	omit). With neither it is unproven, and a stub that shows the other
738	behavior is unproven whatever was stated. A body member the connector guards
739	with `?` (`$args.x?`) drops a null and an absent argument and nothing else:
740	an empty string, empty list, `false` and `0` are still sent, and a null
741	inside a kept object stays, so prove the drop with a case passing an explicit
742	null behind an exact stub. A request-direction omit decision
743	(`decisions add --omit`) removes an optional source body member from this
744	proof, because the record says why the connector does not send it; a member
745	the source marks required is never removed by one and stays a gap
746	(`required_member_omitted`, naming the decision), root omit (`.`) included. An argument the reader cannot place (a method chain, `??`) is
747	placed by execution when an executed, passing case's stub demands the
748	argument's own value at exactly one body pointer in the request that case
749	makes; the expression is not read. The value must be distinctive: a value
750	found at several pointers, a boolean, a short number or string, or the same
751	value as another argument's in the same case is `ambiguous_value` — give the
752	argument a different value in the case (the stub follows). A value the
753	connector reshapes (a date, a casing) is not found and stays
754	`unproven_mapping`: record why or restructure the mapping, never read it as
755	covered. `graphos-factory-core serialization --json` lists each argument's
756	`placements` (`static` or `executed`, with the proving case).
757	
758	A member under a list of input objects (`input.tags.id`, where `tags` is
759	`[TagInput]`) is proven at each element's own index, not at a pointer
760	without one: every element the case passes with the member must be
761	demanded with that value at `/tags/0/id`, `/tags/1/id`, …, the same
762	every-element rule a scalar list argument is held to, and at least one
763	element must carry it; an element the case passes without the member
764	demands nothing. A list inside an element is indexed the same way
765	(`/lines/1/options/0/code`). A gap names the pointer its stub must demand
766	(`body /tags/1/id`). A top-level list of input objects the connector
767	places member by member (`tags: $args.tags { id name }`) is proven the same
768	way; one it forwards whole is still proven by the exact match of the whole
769	array at its pointer.
770	
771	Same-run evidence contract: the layer takes the CURRENT
772	`evidence` run's own `wiremock_e2e` status and log — built earlier in the
773	same invocation — never `.factory/evidence/latest.json` on disk, which
774	mid-run still holds the *previous* run's file. Its per-case verdicts
775	(`pass` / `fail` / `unproven`) land in `case_proofs` on `wiremock_e2e`'s own
776	evidence-layer entry, additive to the existing integer `cases`. Run
777	`e2e.sh` (or `evidence`) first on a pilot, which commits no logs, or every
778	case reads not recorded.
